units.la: His Magiæ specieb. imbuti multa faciunt, quæ nullo modo per causas & media naturalia effici potuerunt, sed necessario referri debent ad substantiam aliquam incorporeám,quæ occulte cum ipsis magis operatur: faciunt enim statuas è ligno vel alia materia loqui, & ad propositas quæstiones respondere, moverique loco progressivo: deinde manifestant etiam quædam occultissima, & quæ humana eis ratione nota esse non potuerunt, ut res quæ geruntur, vel dicuntur in remotissimis regionibus,quæq; quis dixit vel fecit: Hæc autem esse mentis cujusdam sublimioris opera, quàm est humana, prædictasq; operationes non perfici causis naturalibus, sed supra omnis corporeæ naturæ potestatem esse necesse est. Vera Magia & naturalis, quæ causis nititur naturalibus, licet non ita sensui obviis,sed abditioribus& reconditis, ditis, nihil alind est, quàm lapidum, quám herbarum, quàm mineralium, quàm animalium, quàm astrorum cum his consensus vel dissidii scientia, quam exactè callere & didicisse sapientiæ opus est, legi diuinæ non contrarium.
units.tr: Those who are steeped in these kinds of magic do many things that could in no way be brought about through natural causes and means, and must necessarily be referred to some incorporeal substance which works secretly with them. For they make statues of wood or other material speak, answer the questions put to them, and move from place to place; further, they also reveal certain most hidden things, which they could not know by human reason, such as things that are being done or said in the most distant regions, and what anyone has said or done. Now these are the works of a mind higher than the human, and it must be that such operations are not performed by natural causes but lie beyond the power of all corporeal nature. True and natural magic, which rests on natural causes, though not such as are obvious to the senses but hidden and recondite, is nothing other than the knowledge of the sympathy or antipathy of stones, herbs, minerals, animals and stars with one another, a knowledge which a man of wisdom must learn and master exactly, and which is not contrary to the divine law.

units.la: Et hanc magiam quam omnes sapientes, rerumq; cœlestium & sublunarium solertissimi indagatores semper approbarunt, vt quæ in operum Dei admirationem explorantem ducat, qui callent, multarum abstrusissimarum rerum scientia clarebunt, quamuis paucos hodie inuenias, qui exactam huius cognitionem habeant, nisi perditos quosdam ardeliones, qui ob pecuniæ aucupium animas dæmonibus devouent, mentiri non erubescunt, omnia se scire & præscire gloriantes, sicq; veram magiam nefandis nugis desœdantes, & cum Goëtia confundentes.
units.tr: This magic, which all the wise men and the most skilful investigators of heavenly and sublunary things have always approved, since it leads those who understand it to admire the works of God, will shine with the knowledge of many abstruse things. Yet today you will find few who have an exact knowledge of it, except certain ruined charlatans who, hunting for money, devote souls to demons, are not ashamed to lie, boasting that they know and foresee everything, and so defile true magic with unspeakable trifles and confuse it with goëtia.

units.la: Cæterum, quod in præsenti nostro instituto minimè prætereundum fuit, non parum enim lucis afferet & veritatis, ad mysterium nostrum vlterius explicandum, in experimentis non fallacib. est, operationem aliquam esse & virtutem annulorum confectorum ex auro, argento, auricalco, aut quouis metallo, stellæ, cuius quis sibi virtutem conciliare cupit, dedicato, defixo in annuli cavitatem cum subiecta herba stellæ huic Sympathetica, lapide: his enim animum exhilarari, morbosque profligari graues autores tradunt, Trallianus, Gordonius, Mesue & alii.
units.tr: Moreover, what must not be passed over in our present undertaking, since it will bring no little light and truth to the further explanation of our mystery, is that in experiments that do not deceive, there is some operation and virtue in rings made of gold, silver, brass or any metal dedicated to a star whose virtue someone wishes to win, with a stone sympathetic to that star and with the herb placed under it fixed in the hollow of the ring. For serious authors, Trallianus, Gordonius, Mesue and others, report that by these the spirits are cheered and grave diseases are driven off.

units.la: Sic Gyges Lydorum rex annulo suo lapidem Draconis capite exemtum incluserat, sese, Regem & astantes occisurus, vt impune cum Regina concumberet, inuisibilem reddidit. Et Alexander Trallianus Herculis imaginem Leonem suffocantis annulo inclusam colicis mederi scribit. Ferunt & Eudæmum Philosophum annulos contra serpentum morsus, fascinationes & morbos concinnasse. Tradit quoque Iosephus l. 8. antiquit. c. 2. Se vidisse præsente Vespasiano Imperatore, Eleazarum quendam de gente Hebræa, naribus cuiusdam obsessi, annulum, cuius signaculo radix à Salomone reperta, erat subdita, applicuisse, dæmonemq; de naribus odorantis extraxisse, qui cum repente in terram concidisset, Eleazar coniurationis Salomonis Cantico dæmonium proscripsit. Idem Salomonem Magiæ fuisse peritissimum, & Moisen Hebræorum legislatorem in Ægypto Magiæ initiatum annulos amoris & obliuionis fecisse, annulumque obliuionis dedisse Æthiopissæ, vt ipsius obliuisceretur, quo etiam facto in Aegyptum liberè ipsum remigrasse prodidit, non quidem superstitiosa dæmonum magia, cuius eum accusabant Apollonius & Lysimachus, verum à Iosepho propterea refutati, sed ea, quæ per sacrosancta nomina & precationes, ang lorumq; bonorum implorationem perfi-ciebatur. Testes Eusebiu de præpar. Euang. l. 8. c. 2. Iosephus contra Appion. in Act. Apost. c. 7. Plin. l. 3. c. 1. Magian quoq; ab Ægyptio-rum sacerdotibus didicisse & calluisse Empe-doclem, Pythagoram, Democritum & ipsum Platonem in confesso est.
units.tr: Thus Gyges, king of the Lydians, had enclosed in his ring a stone taken from the head of a dragon, and by it made himself invisible, so that he might commit adultery with the queen with impunity, intending to kill the king and those standing by. Alexander of Tralles writes that an image of Hercules strangling a lion, enclosed in a ring, cures colic. They also report that the philosopher Eudaemus made rings against the bites of serpents, against fascinations and against diseases. Josephus also relates, in Antiquities book 8, chapter 2, that in the presence of the Emperor Vespasian he saw a certain Eleazar, of the Hebrew nation, apply to the nostrils of a man possessed a ring whose seal held a root discovered by Solomon, and draw the demon out through the nostrils of the one who was breathing it in; when the man suddenly fell to the ground, Eleazar banished the demon by the incantation composed by Solomon. The same writer reports that Solomon was most skilled in magic, and that Moses, the lawgiver of the Hebrews, initiated in magic in Egypt, made rings of love and of forgetfulness, and gave the ring of forgetfulness to an Ethiopian woman so that she would forget him; by this means he also freely returned to Egypt. Not indeed by the superstitious demonic magic of which Apollonius and Lysimachus accused him, and which Josephus therefore refuted, but by that which was accomplished through the most sacred names, prayers and the invocation of good angels. Witnesses: Eusebius, De praeparatione evangelica, book 8, chapter 2; Josephus, Against Apion; Act. Apost. c. 7; Pliny, book 3, chapter 1. It is admitted that Empedocles, Pythagoras, Democritus and Plato himself learned magic and mastered it from the priests of Egypt.

units.la: Vnde non omninò vana esse elicitur, quæ de cura characteristica, quæ sculptis imagi-nibus & de collo appensis naturales operationes perficit per cœlestes proprietates siderum mi-rabili influentia cum nostris corporibus con-cordantium, non inquam plane vana sunt, quæ antiquissimi naturæ explorato-res de verbo scri-pto seu characteribus & sigillis, certis tempori-bus secundum cœli virtutem & influxum fa-brefactis, citra omnem, quam sola mysterii huius ignorantia finxit, superstitionem, citra nominis divini prophanationem & offendi-culum, vllamq; fidei ac religionis violationem, literis monimentisq; confecrarunt, quæ licet hactenus postremisq; hilce temporibus occul-tata & abscondita delituerunt, altoq; silentio compressa apud quosdam, qui illis sunt abusi potius quam legitime vsi, cum ad superstitio-nes prolapsi, primordia non intelligentes, plus iis tribuere sunt ausi, quàm rerum omnium creator Deus concessit, voluitque esse per ea patepatefacta; Tantum vero abest, vt hiscę imaginibus per se virium quid tribuam, characteresq; seu nomina constellata virtutem habere ratione figurę, affirmem (cum figura, numerus, magnitudo, situs, continuiq; solutio nullius sunt actionis principia) vt, nisi aliud sit agēs mouensque, cuius potestate characteres sunt efficaces, plane negem. Tamen inuidiæ fenestra patefacta lucem ea videre sum passus, vt cognitio veri, quæ bonum quoddam & perfectio intellectus est, elucescat, ac clarius cernatur, quantum inter veras & physicas signaturas & superstitiosas ac illicitas interfit, tum speculatiuè & noscendi tantum causâ, non etiam vtendi & exercendi modo quædam scire licitum esse & concessum. Nulla enim virtus vel in cœlo vel in terra, quæ non descendat à Deo: sic medicamenta sunt corpora visibilia, verba corpora inuisibilia, siue herba siue verbum sanet, in causa est Deus, id est, spiritus Dei naturæ coadunatus per verbum fiat. Vnde ipsa herba non est medicina, sed hæc in illa latet inuisibiliter à Deo videlicet insita. Quapropter non protinus ad orcum vsq; sunt damnanda, insulseq; deridenda, quæ à sensibus sunt remotiora, & causas habent abstrusas. Gemmarum miracula quis non obstupescit? Plurimas certè iis inesse facultates naturales negari non potest nec debet, præsertim si certis sub constellationibus nibus sculptæ, imaginibusq; ac signaturis impressæ fuerint & signatæ. Ac plane vanum est, quod quidam putant, effectus gemmarum quarundam prouenire vi magica, nec naturales esse, proficisciqué ex Magorum schola, qui prætextum suis veneficiis quærant per gemmas certis constellationibus sculptas. Smaragdum mortui Domini digitis, quibus fuit gestatus, obsilire, cognitum est & compertum. Turcosiæ quoq; vires quis nō miratur? Et innumera possunt non tantum gemmarum, sed etiam plantarum experimenta coaceruari, quæ si non vbiq;, & semper respondent, non arguenda ideò sunt mendacii, quia non omnia vbiq; & semper concurrunt, & raritas effectus seu singularitas effectus non tollit causam in natura. Rerum enim miracula perpetrantur per debitam causarum naturalium agentium cum dispositis patientibus applicatione, adeò occulte, vt causa videatur remotissima. Itaq; vesanum est diabolicis machinamentis protinus ascribere, quæ à nostris sensibus sunt remotiora, non cogitantes, latentem naturæ vim quæ diuinum diuinæ potentiæ est instrumentum, multum posse sine diabolorum ope & auxilio. Sic vesani sunt, qui superstitionibus dediti etiam manifestissima pene præ ignorantia aut stolida dubitatione, ex occultis prodire causis asserunt, vt in eodem vesaniæ pelago nauigant, qui præter odorem colorem & saporem nullas alias vires plantis quibusdam inesse arbitrantur, quasi naturalis illa coelestium cum elementaribus conspiratio efficere non possit, vt praeter qualitates primas tactiles & sensuales occultas etiam vires possi-deat sine magicis incantamentis anili & super-stitione, id quod naturales cum experientia ef-sectus demonstrant. Quare in singulari facto, non aliam praeterquam quae nobis videtur es-se, statuere causam, temerarium duco. Quis e-nim negare potest, diuinitus aut genii alicuius virtute, aut etiam causis accidentariis & fortui-tis, posse produci effectum similem naturali. Et sufficit Physico ostendisse effectum similem vel talem esse causarum naturalium, aut sem-per aut plerunq;. Et licet non semper respon-deat euentus, non tamen ideo naturae motus est denegandus, siquidem ad vnum saepe esse-ctum raro concurrunt causae omnes, quod li-cet ex illis aestimare, quae ob raritatem, varietate & singularitatem pro miraculis habentur & prodigiis, haec enim causas habent naturales, raro tamen ad effectum talem dispositas, aut o-mnes paratas. Itaq; si effectus est naturalis, et-iam causa talis erit, & contra. Iam a.imaginum sub certis astris sculptarum effectus naturalis omnino est, ergo causam quoq; naturalem esse necesse est. Licet vero haec sit occulta & abstru-sa, atq; sensibus exterioribus remotior, non tatamen illico ad diabolicam quandam potestatem confugiendum, sed attendendum, quibus auxiliis quibusque causis concurrentibus fiat aut non fiat effectus, èq; mirabilib. causis naturalibus q; effectis mirabilis potius Dei potentia agnoscenda & praedicanda, qui cum tantas virtutes tamque mirabiles in naturam manifestam insevit, quantus, dic amabo te, ipse in suis occultis erit? His ita praestratis, pro vita salubriter producenda, honoribusq; ac diuitiis augmentandis Iouis sigillum atq; imago fabricatur sculpiturq; in lapide albo vel claro, vel etiam argento puro aut stanno, ipso tamen Ioue, quod inprimis in hoc mysterio obseruandum est, existente vel in suo domicilio, vt sagittario vel piscibus, vel etiam exaltatione, vt Cancro, libero ab omnib. impedimentis, praecipue vero a radiis malis Saturni vel Martis: in angulo etiam sit orientis vel Medio Caeli, ascendens in circulo augis, directus, velox cursu, non a solle combustus, orientalis in gradib. lucidis & fortunam augentib. in Lunae vel Veneris trigono aut sextili, quae omnia diligentissime ab Astrologiae perito obseruari necesse est.
units.tr: Hence it follows that what is said about the characteristic cure is not wholly vain. That cure, by the wonderful influence of the heavenly properties of the stars, which agree with our bodies, produces natural effects through images carved and hung from the neck. Nor, I say, are the things entirely vain which the most ancient explorers of nature consecrated in writings and monuments: the written word, or characters and seals, made at certain times according to the power and influence of heaven. These, free from all the superstition that ignorance of this mystery alone has invented, and free from any profanation of the divine name, stumbling block, or violation of faith and religion, were recorded in letters and monuments. Although they have been hidden and concealed until now, and in these latter times have lain buried in deep silence among some who have abused them rather than used them lawfully, having fallen into superstitions, not understanding their beginnings, and dared to ascribe to them more than God, the Creator of all things, granted and willed to be made manifest through them. I am so far from attributing any power in itself to these images, or affirming that characters or constellated names have virtue by reason of their figure (since figure, number, magnitude, position and continuity or separation are not principles of any action), that I would plainly deny it, unless there were another agent and mover by whose power the characters are efficacious. Yet, since a window has been opened to envy, I have allowed these things to come to light, so that the knowledge of truth, which is a certain good and perfection of the intellect, may shine forth and be seen more clearly: how great the difference is between true, natural signatures and superstitious and illicit ones; and that it is lawful and permitted to know certain things speculatively, and for the sake of knowing only, not also for the manner of using and practising them. For there is no virtue in heaven or on earth that does not descend from God. Thus medicines are visible bodies, and words are invisible bodies. Whether an herb or a word heals, God is the cause, that is, the Spirit of God, joined to nature, works through the word. Hence the herb itself is not the medicine, but the medicine lies hidden invisibly in it, implanted there by God. Therefore those things which are more remote from our senses and have hidden causes are not to be condemned at once to hell, nor foolishly mocked. Who is not amazed at the wonders of gems? It cannot be denied, and ought not to be denied, that they possess very many natural faculties, especially if they have been carved under certain constellations and impressed and marked with images and signatures. And it is plainly vain what some think: that the effects of certain gems come from magical power and are not natural, and proceed from the school of the Magi, who seek a pretext for their poisons in gems carved under certain constellations. That the emerald cleaves to the fingers of a dead lord on which it was worn is known and established. Who does not marvel at the powers of turquoise? Innumerable experiments, not only of gems but also of plants, could be heaped together. If these do not answer everywhere and always, they are not therefore to be charged with falsehood, because not all things concur everywhere and always; and the rarity or singularity of an effect does not remove its cause in nature. For the wonders of things are brought about through the due application of natural causes to suitably disposed patients, so secretly that the cause seems very remote. It is therefore madness to ascribe at once to diabolical contrivances what is more remote from our senses, not considering that the hidden power of nature, which is the instrument of divine power, can do much without the help and assistance of devils. Those are equally mad who, given to superstitions, out of ignorance or foolish doubt, assert that even the most manifest effects arise from hidden causes; they sail in the same sea of madness as those who think that certain plants have no powers beyond smell, colour and taste, as if that natural conspiracy of the heavenly bodies with the elementary ones could not bring it about that, besides the primary tactile and sensible qualities, they also possess hidden powers, without magical incantations, old wives' tales and superstition, which natural effects demonstrate with experience. Therefore I consider it rash to posit, in a single fact, any other cause than the one that appears to us. For who can deny that an effect similar to a natural one may be produced by divine power, or by the virtue of some spirit, or even by accidental and chance causes? And it is enough for the natural philosopher to have shown that an effect similar to such a one is the result of natural causes, either always or for the most part. And although the outcome does not always answer, the natural motion is not therefore to be denied; for all the causes seldom concur to produce one effect. This can be judged from those things which, because of their rarity, variety and singularity, are held to be miracles and prodigies; for these have natural causes, which are rarely disposed to produce such an effect, or all ready at once. Thus, if the effect is natural, the cause will also be natural, and conversely. Now the effect of images carved under certain stars is wholly natural; therefore its cause must also be natural. Although this cause is hidden and abstruse, and more remote from the outward senses, we must not at once flee to some diabolical power, but attend to what helps and what concurrent causes bring about or prevent the effect. From these wonderful natural causes and effects the power of God, which is more wonderful, is rather to be acknowledged and proclaimed. For since he has planted such great and marvellous virtues in manifest nature, how great, I ask you, will he himself be in his hidden things? With these things thus set forth, for prolonging life healthfully and increasing honours and riches, the seal and image of Jupiter is made and carved on white or clear stone, or even on pure silver or tin; but Jupiter himself, which must above all be observed in this mystery, must be present, either in his own house, as in Sagittarius or Pisces, or else in exaltation, as in Cancer, free from all impediments, and especially from the evil rays of Saturn or Mars. He should also be in the angle of the East or Midheaven, rising in the circle of the augs, direct, swift in course, not burnt by the sun, oriental, in bright degrees that increase fortune, in the trine or sextile of the Moon or Venus. All these things must be observed most diligently by one skilled in astrology.

units.la: Sic idem Iupiter contrarium operabitur, si retrogradus fuerit, combustus, afflictus a Saturno vel Marte, in malo caeli loco, non in domicilio vel exaltatione, &c. Idemque iudicium esto de caeteris etiam Planetis:
units.tr: Thus the same Jupiter will work the contrary if he is retrograde, burnt, afflicted by Saturn or Mars, in an evil place of the heavens, not in his house or exaltation, etc. The same judgement is to be made of the other planets also.

units.tr: N.B.

units.la: In sigillis conficiendis quid ne cessario obseruandu?
units.tr: What must necessarily be observed in making seals?

units.la: Eundem in modum fabricatur Imago Martis in 1. facie Scorpionis orientis, contra timiditatem & pusillanimitatem.
units.tr: The image of Mars is made in the same manner, in the first face of Scorpio rising, against timidity and pusillanimity.

units.la: Ad fauorem Regum & principum conciliandum, morbosq; calidos cordiales curandos, Imago Solis in auro puro prima Leonis facie ascendente: ipse vero Sol in Leone sit fortis & fortunatus:
units.tr: To win the favour of kings and princes, and to cure hot cordial diseases, the image of the Sun is made in pure gold, with the first face of Leo ascending; the Sun himself should be in Leo, strong and fortunate.

units.la: Ad laetitiam, venustatem roburque corporis imago Veneris poma floresq; tenentis manu ascendente cum ea prima facie Librae, Piscium vel tauri,
units.tr: For joy, beauty and bodily strength, the image of Venus holding apples and flowers in her hand is made, with the first face of Libra, Pisces or Taurus ascending together with her.

units.la: Ad ingenium & memoriam acuendam imago Mercurii orientis cum prima geminorum facie vel Virginis: vel contra morbos, odia, & itinera feliciter conficienda a gradu 17. Virginis usq; ad finem fere eiusdem signi:
units.tr: To sharpen the wit and memory, the image of Mercury rising with the first face of Gemini or Virgo is made; or against diseases, hatreds and to bring journeys to a happy end, from the 17th degree of Virgo almost to the end of the same sign.

units.la: Ad podagram curandam, indubitanter valere piscium figuram in auro vel argento, seu auro argento permixto, sculptā, sole permeante Piscesin ascēdente aut domo decima, ab infortuniis saluo & libero, domino etiā signi videlicet Iouę Saluo: vel etiā Luna mediū cœli tenente, Marte non præsente, & Iouę non retrogrado, Soleq; supra terrā existente, si piscium imago fiat in prima piscium facie, eundem præstare effectum antiquissimis monimentis proditum reperitur: in secunda vero facie factam sanare tibiarum morbos, in tertia morbos genuum & coxarum:
units.tr: For curing gout, the figure of a fish, carved in gold or silver, or in a mixture of gold and silver, is undoubtedly effective, with the Sun passing through Pisces, Pisces ascending or in the tenth house, safe and free from misfortunes, and with the lord of the sign, namely Jupiter, safe. Or else, with the Moon holding the midheaven, Mars not present, Jupiter not retrograde, and the Sun above the earth, if the image of the fish is made in the first face of Pisces, it is found in the most ancient monuments to produce the same effect; but made in the second face, it cures diseases of the shins, and in the third, diseases of the knees and hips.

units.la: Ad morbos gulæ & colli faciebant figuram tauri in facie tertia, Sole existente supra terram, eamq; in cupro multum rubente.
units.tr: For diseases of the throat and neck they made the figure of a bull in the third face, with the sun above the earth, and cast it in copper that is strongly reddened.

units.la: Ad morbos capitis difficiles & difficulter curabiles, fabricatur figura arietis, Martis & Saturni, vtroq; existente directo, Ioue non constituto in ariete, nec Venere in Scorpio, nec Mercurio in tauro, à gradu primo vsq; ad 5. primæ faciei arietis: Sole autem existente in ariete eandem obtinebit virtutem.
units.tr: For difficult diseases of the head, hard to cure, a figure of a ram is made, of Mars and Saturn, both being direct, with Jupiter not placed in Aries, nor Venus in Scorpio, nor Mercury in Taurus, from the first degree up to the fifth of the first face of Aries; but if the sun is in Aries, it will have the same power.

units.la: Ad bona & honores adipiscendos, morbosque celebri frigidos curandos imaginem Lunæ conferre in purissimo argento vel crystallo, ita vt Luna existat in Cancro, aque infortunis sit libera, in oriente fortis & fortunata, experimentis patefactum esse Doctores antiqui asserunt, adq; eundem quoq; effectum consequendum positus eiusdem in tauro efficax est, quo in signo exaltatur:
units.tr: For obtaining goods and honours, and for curing diseases that are commonly cold, the image of the moon is to be made in very pure silver or crystal, so that the moon is in Cancer, free from malefic influences, strong and fortunate in the east; the ancient teachers assert that this has been revealed by experience, and that a position of the same in Taurus, where it is exalted, is also effective for obtaining the same effect.

units.la: Ad ventris ægritudines curandas figura Cancri facta hora Saturni, cancro existente in medio cœli, & Saturno in secunda facie, omni auro præstare dicitur, omnibus morbis resistendis expellendisq; idonea.
units.tr: For curing diseases of the belly, a figure of Cancer is made at the hour of Saturn, with Cancer in the midheaven and Saturn in the second face; it is said to surpass all gold, and to be suitable for resisting and driving out all diseases.

units.la: Ad tristitiam abigendam & melancholicam desipientiam, figuram Capricorni prodesse prodictum est, ita tamen, vt Mercurius non sit retrogradus, sitq; cum Venere supra terram, Venus autem sit in parte orientali, Saturnus verò sub terra: conficiendum autem sigillum est in prima facie, Solis aut Mercurii die, Solis tamen hora:
units.tr: For driving away sadness and melancholic folly, it is declared that a figure of Capricorn is useful, provided that Mercury is not retrograde and is with Venus above the earth, Venus being in the eastern part, and Saturn below the earth; the seal is to be made in the first face, on a day of the Sun or Mercury, but at an hour of the Sun.

units.la: Adsensum corruptum & deperditum, morbosq; manuum inprimis dextræ commendari video Imaginem Sagittarii factam de auro vel argento in prima facie primi gradus vsq; ad 5. die Solis & hora eius: hæc figura habet vim expellendi infirmitates, Saturni, Veneris & Martis, oportet autem Saturnum non esse retrogradum, nec Martem in 12. domo, sicut nec Iovem in quarta. Sol vero supra terram existat.
units.tr: For corrupted and lost sense, and especially for diseases of the hands, particularly the right, I find it recommended: an image of Sagittarius made of gold or silver in the first face, from the first degree up to the fifth, on a day and hour of the Sun. This figure has the power of driving out the infirmities of Saturn, Venus and Mars; it is necessary, however, that Saturn not be retrograde, nor Mars in the twelfth house, nor Jupiter in the fourth. The Sun should be above the earth.

units.la: Atq; hæc sunt sigilla & sculptura Planetarum & constellationum quarundam Cœlestium, à diuersis autoribus repertæ, sequuntur ordine, quæ in antiquissimorum Sophorum & Doctorum monumentis & Codicibus, & à verbo ad verbum huc transcriptæ, consignatæ imagines inueniuntur, quæ multarum mirandarumq; virium esse perhibentur, si in convenientibus lapidib. sculptæ magna cum reverentia, & deuotione (sed absit superstitio) gestentur & custodiantur: & primo quidem inter vetustissimi illius & summi Rhagaelis arcana fuerunt.
units.tr: These are the seals and engravings of certain Planets and celestial constellations, reported by various authors; they follow in order, and are found as images written down word for word from the monuments and codices of the most ancient wise men and teachers. They are said to have many marvellous powers, if they are engraved in suitable stones and carried and kept with great reverence and devotion (but far be superstition). And first of all they were among the secrets of that most ancient and supreme Rhagael.

units.la: Draconis formosi imago, si in Rubino siue in alio lapide similis naturæ sculpta fuerit, scias virtutem eius esse in augendis bonis huius seculi, gestantemq; hilarem & sanum efficere. Falconis imago, si in Topatio sit, ad acqui- rendam beneuolentiam Regum, principum & magnatum facit.
units.tr: The image of a beautiful dragon, if it is engraved in a ruby or another stone of similar nature, you should know its power is in increasing the goods of this age, and it makes the wearer cheerful and healthy. The image of a falcon, if it is in a topaz, wins the goodwill of kings, princes and great men.

units.la: Astrolabii imago si in Granato sculpta fuerit, virtus eius erit, sanum reddere gestantem, & ab omnibus ægritudinibus, aduersisque casibus in itinere liberum.
units.tr: The image of an astrolabe, if engraved in a garnet, its power will be to make the wearer healthy, and free from all sicknesses and adverse chances on a journey.

units.la: Asini imago, si in Chrysolito sit, virtus eius erit futura prognosticare & prædicere. (quantum sc. potest euadere in humanam imbecillitatem, verè enim futura prædicere solius est Dei.
units.tr: The image of an ass, if it is in a chrysolite, its power will be to foretell and predict (as far as it can escape human weakness; for truly to foretell the future belongs to God alone).

units.la: Arietis vel capitis hominis cum barba imago in sapphyro sculpta virtutem habet sanandi, & liberandi à multis infirmitatibus, & à carcere, omniq; molestia, estq; imago regia, dat enim dignitates & honores, ac in altum extollit.
units.tr: An image of a ram, or of a human head with a beard, engraved in a sapphire, has the power of healing and freeing from many infirmities, and from prison and every trouble; and it is a royal image, for it gives dignities and honours and raises one on high.

units.la: Ranæ figura si in berillo sculpta erit, virtutem habet inimicos reconciliandi, & amicitiam inter homines, si discordes ipsâ tetigeris.
units.tr: The figure of a frog, if it is engraved in a beryl, has the power of reconciling enemies and friendship between men, if you touch those who are at odds with it.

units.la: Camelini capitis, vel duarum caprarum inter myrrhi arbores imago si in Onyche sit, virtutem habet conuocandi, congregandi, & constringendi dæmonas, si quis secum portaucrit, & in somnio facit terribilia videre ac mirabilia.
units.tr: The image of a camel's head, or of two goats among myrrh trees, if it is in an onyx, has the power of summoning, gathering and binding demons, if anyone carries it with him, and it makes them see terrible and marvellous things in dreams.

units.la: Vulturis imago si in Chrysolito sit, virtus tus eius erit dæmones frenare & congregare, defendere locum,in quo ponitur à malis spiritibus,& ab eorum infestatione, gestantiq; dæmones facit obedientes.
units.tr: The image of a vulture, if it is in a chrysolite, its power will be to restrain and gather demons, to defend the place in which it is placed from evil spirits and their molestation, and it makes demons obedient to the wearer.

units.la: Vespertilionis imago si in Heliotropio sculpta erit, gestanti potentiam dat resistendi dæmonibus.
units.tr: The image of a bat, if it is engraved in a heliotrope, gives the wearer power of resisting demons.

units.la: Hominis bene ornati imago & habentis aliquid pulcri in manibus, si in Cornelio sculpta erit, virtutem habebit stringendi sanguinem, & ad honores confert.
units.tr: The image of a well-dressed man holding something beautiful in his hands, if engraved in a cornelian, will have the power of stopping blood, and it brings honours.

units.la: Leonis vel Sagittarij imago, si in lapide sit, ad venena valet,& à febre liberat.
units.tr: The image of a lion or of Sagittarius, if it is in a stone, is good against poisons and frees from fever.

units.la: Hominis armati cum arca & sagitta imago si in iride sculpta fuerit, virtutem habet custodire gestantem, & loca, in quibus versatur, à malo.
units.tr: The image of an armed man with a bow and arrow, if engraved in an iris, has the power to guard the wearer and the places in which he moves from evil.

units.la: Hominis imago cum ense in manu, si in Cornelio sit, virtutem habet præseruare locum in quo erit, à fulgure & tempestate, & gestantem à vitiis, & à fascinatione custodit.
units.tr: The image of a man with a sword in his hand, if it is in a cornelian, has the power to protect the place in which it is from lightning and storm, and guards the wearer from vices and from fascination.

units.la: Tauri imago si in Prassio sit,ad maleficia iuuare dicitur,& in magisteriis gratiam præbet.
units.tr: The image of a bull, if it is in a prasius, is said to help against evil arts, and it gives favour in magical undertakings.

units.la: Vpupæ figura cum Dragontea herba ante se,si in Beryllo sit, virtutem habebit aquaticos prouocare spiritus, & loqui cohibere, deque quæsitis ab eis responsa recipere.
units.tr: A figure of a hoopoe with the dragonwort herb before it, if it is in a beryl, will have the power of summoning water spirits, restraining speech, and receiving answers from them to questions put to them.

units.la: Hominis imago cum dextra manu erecta ad cœlum,si in Chalcedonio sit, virtus eius erit vincere ciuiles lites, & gestantem reddere fa-num, & in itineribus, ac à caulis noxiis præ-feruare.
units.tr: The image of a man with his right hand raised to heaven, if it is in a chalcedony, its power will be to win civil lawsuits, to make the wearer healthy, and to protect him on journeys and from harmful accidents.

units.la: Dei nomina in Ceraunia si sculpta fuerint, virtutem habebit præseruare loca, in quibus exit hæc imago, à tempestatibus, & poten-tiam victoriamque dare gestantibus contra i-nimicos suos.
units.tr: If the names of God are engraved on a ceraunia, it will have the power to protect the places in which this image is from storms, and to give power and victory to those who carry it against their enemies.

units.la: Vrsi imago si in Amethysto sit fugiendi dæ-mones virtutem haber,& hominem ab ebrie-tate defendendi & præseruandi.
units.tr: The image of a bear, if it is in an amethyst, has the power of putting demons to flight, and of defending and preserving a man from drunkenness.

units.la: Hominis armati Imago in magnete sculpta, gestantes in bello reddit victoriosos. Hacte-nus Rhagael.
units.tr: An image of an armed man engraved in a magnet makes those who carry it victorious in war. So far Rhagael.

units.la: IMAGINES SEV SIGILLA Chaelis.
units.tr: Images or Seals of Chael.

units.la: CHael vnus ex filiis filiorum Israel, anti-quissimus Doctor, cum in deserto esset, obseruauit,& sculpere fecit multas secundum cursum signorum & planetarum figuras, & maximum effectum in eis agnouit, vtque hæ imaginum virtutes posteris paterent, librum composuit, ex quo sequentia sunt excerpta Sitq; benedictus Deus, qui terris tales virtutes dedit in salutem humani generis. (Hæc verba reperinntur in ipso libro à Chaele conscripto statim in principio.) HomiHominis figura sedentis post aratrum, cum longa barba, vultuque longo & supercilijs curuatis, in cuius collo sint quatuor homines iacentes, & qui teneat in manibus vulpē & vulturem, si talis lapis, in quo haec erunt sculpta, collo suspendatur, ad omnes plantationes valet, & ad inueniendum thesauros, nam si sub ceruice iturus in lectum posueris, in somno videbis thesauros, ac modum extrahendi: est & alia eius virtus, scilicet conferre aegritudinibus brutorum, cum aquam biberunt, in qua hic lapis lotus fuerit, debet autem sculpi in die & hora Veneris.
units.tr: Chael, one of the sons of the sons of Israel, a very ancient teacher, while he was in the desert, observed the courses of the signs and planets, had many figures carved according to them, and recognised their greatest effect. So that the virtues of these images might be made known to posterity, he composed a book, from which the following passages are excerpted. May God be blessed, who has given such virtues to the earth for the salvation of the human race. (These words are found in the book written by Chael himself, at the very beginning.) The figure of a man sitting behind a plough, with a long beard, a long face and arched eyebrows, with four men lying on his neck, and holding a fox and a vulture in his hands: if such a stone, with these figures carved on it, is hung from the neck, it is good for all planting and for finding treasures. For if you place it under your head when you are about to go to bed, you will see treasures in your sleep, and the way of extracting them. It has another virtue as well, namely to help the sicknesses of beasts: when they drink the water in which this stone has been washed. It must be carved on the day and hour of Venus.

units.la: Hominis imago habentis in collo clypeum, & in capite galeam tenentis in manu gladium, ac conculcantis sub pedibus serpentem, in Iaspide rubeo sculpta, si collo suspedatur, omnes superabit inimicos in praelio, & maxime si commissum fuerit die Martis.
units.tr: The image of a man wearing a shield on his neck, holding a helmet on his head and a sword in his hand, and trampling a serpent under his feet, carved in red jasper: if it is hung from the neck, it will overcome all enemies in battle, especially if the engagement takes place on a Tuesday.

units.la: Equi imago habentis Crocodilum supra se in hiacyntho sculpta, virtutem habet reddere gestantem victorem in ciuilibus causis, amatum, morigeratum, efficit & amabilem, debetque in auro ligari, quia ex auro virtus eius augmentatur.
units.tr: The image of a horse, with a crocodile above it, carved in hyacinth: it has the power of making the bearer victorious in civil lawsuits, and makes him loved, obliging and agreeable. It should be set in gold, because its virtue is increased by gold.

units.la: Hominis figura sedentis, & mulieris stantis ante eū capillis sparsis versus renes, & viri sursum aspicientis in Cornelio sculpta, virtus eius erit, ab omnibus hoc lapide contactis benebeneuolentiam acquirere: lapidi autem debet suppono parum ambræ,& terebinthinæ.
units.tr: The figure of a seated man and a standing woman before him, with her hair loose down to her loins, and a man looking upward, carved in cornelian: its virtue is that all who touch this stone acquire goodwill. A little ambergris and turpentine should be placed under the stone.

units.la: Equi spumantis & feruidi, super quem vir niger sedeat cum sceptro in manu, figura sculpta in hemathite, regnandi potestatem prębet, & amissam gratiam restaurat, debetq; in æquali pondere auri & argenti ligari.
units.tr: The figure of a foaming and fiery horse, with a black man sitting on it holding a sceptre in his hand, carved in haematite: it grants the power to rule and restores lost favour. It should be set in gold and silver of equal weight.

units.la: Hominis sedentis cum accensa candela in manu imago, si in Chrysolito sculpta fuerit, gestantem diuitem efficit, debetq; in purissimo auro ligari.
units.tr: The image of a seated man holding a lit candle in his hand, if carved in chrysolite, makes the wearer rich. It should be set in the purest gold.

units.la: Cerui aut venatoris, aut canis, aut leporis figura sculpta, virtutem habet frenandi dæmones, lunaticos, phreneticos.
units.tr: The figure of a stag, or of a hunter, or of a dog, or of a hare, carved: it has the power to restrain demons, lunatics and the frantic.

units.la: Mulieris imaginem habentis in vna manu auem, & in alia piscem sculptam, scias virtutem habere in capiendis piscibus & auibus; debet in argento ligari.
units.tr: The image of a woman holding a bird in one hand and a fish in the other, carved: know that it has power in catching fish and birds. It should be set in silver.

units.la: Imago cuius anterior pars est equus, posterior vero capra, si in aliquo lapide sculpta fit, dat fortunam in alendis & armandis animalibus seu bestiis omnium generum, debetque in plumbo ligari.
units.tr: An image whose front part is a horse and whose hind part is a goat: if it is carved on any stone, it gives good fortune in feeding and equipping animals or beasts of every kind. It should be set in lead.

units.la: Mulieris sedentis cum tuba in equo, seu militis currentis cum cornu ad collum, & cum arbore ante se, figura sculpta in aliquo lapide venatoribus venandi gratiam prabet, si secum portauerint.
units.tr: The figure of a woman sitting on a horse with a trumpet, or of a soldier running with a horn at his neck and a tree before him, carved on some stone: it grants hunters favour in hunting, if they carry it with them.

units.la: Hominis flexis genibus sursum respicientis, & tenentis pannum figura, si in lapide sculpta erit, ac quis secum portauerit, dat gratiam & diuitias in rebus emendis & vendendis.
units.tr: The figure of a man on bended knees looking upward and holding a cloth: if it is carved on a stone, and whoever carries it with him, it gives favour and riches in buying and selling.

units.la: Scorpionis & Sagittarij ad inuicem pugnā-tium figura, si in aliquo lapide sculpta fuerit, maleuolos & discordes efficiet concordes, inimicos amicos, ligetur autem in argento.
units.tr: The figure of a scorpion and a archer fighting against each other, if carved on any stone, will make the malicious and discordant into peaceful people, and enemies into friends. It should be set in silver.

units.la: Vulturis imago cum ramo oliuæ in ore si in pyrite sculpseris, tecumq; portaueris in argen-teo annulo, ad multa conuiuia vocaberis, & omnes te aspicient cum admiratione & stu-pore.
units.tr: If you carve the image of a vulture with an olive branch in its beak in pyrite, and carry it with you in a silver ring, you will be called to many feasts, and everyone will look at you with admiration and amazement.

units.la: Arietis & Leonis medietatis figura, si in ali-quo pretioso lapide sculpta fuerit, si discordes cum ea tetigeris amabiles & concordes effici-entur, debetq; in argento ligari.
units.tr: The figure of the half of a ram and a lion, if carved in any precious stone: if you touch discordant people with it, they will become agreeable and harmonious. It should be set in silver.

units.la: Mulieris in superiore parte, in inferiori vero piscis figura, quę vna manu speculum teneat, & in altera manu ramum, in hiacyntho sculpta, digitoque in annulo aureo gestata, inuisibiles reddit, voluendus autem annulus cum lapide versus palmam est, palmaq; claudenda.
units.tr: The figure of a woman in the upper part, and of a fish in the lower part, who holds a mirror in one hand and a branch in the other, carved in hyacinth and worn on a finger in a gold ring, makes the wearer invisible. The ring must be turned with the stone towards the palm, and the palm must be closed.

units.la: Basilisci, cuius pars vna est fœminæ, inferior vero serpentis figura, si in aliqno preciosorum lapidum sculpta fuerit, virtutem habebit cun-cta fugandi animalia venenosa.
units.tr: The figure of a basilisk, one part of which is a woman, and the lower part a serpent: if it is carved in any precious stone, it will have the power to drive away all poisonous animals.

units.la: Basilisci pugnantis cum Dracone figura, & desuper sit caput hominis in Cornelio sculpta, si collo appendatur, gestanti dabit virtutem superansuperandi omnem bestiam tam terrenam quam marinam.
units.tr: The figure of a basilisk fighting a dragon, with the head of a man above it, carved in cornelian: if it is hung from the neck, it will give the bearer the power to overcome every beast, both land and sea.

units.la: Hominis nudi inflati figura, cum alterius hominis figura bene induti, ac tenentis in vna manu scyplum, in altera vero Ramum herbæ, si in Gagate lapide sculpta fuerit, virtutem habere scias liberandi ab omnibus febribus, si per triduum quis secum portauerit.
units.tr: The figure of a naked, puffed-up man, with the figure of another man well dressed, and holding a staff in one hand and a branch of herb in the other, if carved in jet: know that it has power to free from all fevers, if someone carries it with him for three days.

units.la: Hominis statuam habentis caput bouinum, & pedes aquilæ, sculptam in aliquo lapide si tecum portaueris, nullus hominum de te male loquetur.
units.tr: If you carry with you a statue of a man with the head of an ox and the feet of an eagle, carved in any stone, no one will speak ill of you.

units.la: Hominem flectentem genua, & sursum aspicientem, & manu tenentem, pannum in Turcosia sculptum, scias valere ad emendas & vendendas res.
units.tr: The figure of a man bending his knees and looking upward, holding a cloth in his hand, carved in turquoise: know that it is effective for buying and selling goods.

units.la: Scorpionis & Sagittarij inter se bellantium figura in aliquo lapide sculpta, & ligata in annulo ferreo ceræ impressa, statim inter se discordes efficit, quoscunq; ea tetigeris.
units.tr: The figure of a scorpion and an archer fighting one another, carved in some stone and set in an iron ring, impressed in wax: it at once makes discordant those whom you touch with it.

units.la: Arietis figuram cum medietate bouis in aliqua gemma sculptam, virtutem habere scias, si in annulo argenteo ligata fuerit, ut quoscunque ea tetigeris, confestim tales concordes fiant.
units.tr: Know that the figure of a ram with the half of an ox, carved in some gem, has power if it is set in a silver ring, so that whomever you touch with it are at once made harmonious.

units.la: Fœminæ in superiori & in inferiori parte figura piscis, quæ in vna manu teneat speculū, & in alia ramum, si in Hiacyntho sculpta fuerit, ligataque annulo aureo inuisibilem reddit, quandoquandocunq; volueris: est autem sigillum ce-ra cooperiendum, digitoque palmam versus gestandum.
units.tr: The figure of a fish with a woman in the upper and the lower part, who holds a mirror in one hand and a branch in the other, if carved in hyacinth and set in a gold ring, makes the wearer invisible whenever you wish. The seal must be covered with wax, and it must be worn with the stone turned towards the palm.

units.la: Hominis arantis figura, & supra illum sit manus Domini faciens signum, & iuxta illud sculpta sit stella, si in aliqua gemma sculpta fue-rit, & honestissime gestaueris, in qua regione eris, à tempestate non peribis, & fructus terræ similiter in illa non peribunt.
units.tr: The figure of a man ploughing, and above him a hand of the Lord making a sign, and beside it a star carved: if it is carved in some gem and you wear it most honourably, in whatever region you are, you will not perish by storm, and the fruits of the earth in that place will likewise not perish.

units.la: Viri iuuenis tenentis in capite coronam, & sedentis super thronum quadrupedem, & sub quolibet pede sit vir stans tenens cathedram collo, sitq; circa caput sedentis circulus, & manus eius sint erectæ ad cœlum, si hanc figuram sub Hiacynth o albo sculptam repereris, posue-risq; hunc lapidē in argenteo annulo, in æqua-li pondere ad lapidē, & sub lapide modicū ma-stichis & terebinthinæ, ac feceris sigillum in cera, gestauerisq; ad collum, à Regibus & prin-cipibus impetrabis, quicquid volueris, iustissi-me autem & castissime est gestandus.
units.tr: The figure of a young man wearing a crown on his head, sitting on a throne with four feet, and under each foot a man standing and holding a chair at his neck; and around the head of the seated man a circle, and his hands raised to heaven: if you find this figure carved in white hyacinth, and set this stone in a silver ring, in equal weight to the stone, and under the stone a little mastic and turpentine, and you make a seal in wax, and wear it at your neck, you will obtain from kings and princes whatever you wish. It must be worn most justly and most chastely.

units.la: Serpentis figuram habentis supra dorsum virum, & viro insideat coruus, si in aliquo la-pide sculptam inuenies, qui hunc lapidem se-cum portarit, omnibus abundabit, & erit astu-tus atq; prudens.
units.tr: If you find, carved in some stone, the figure of a serpent with a man on its back, and a raven sitting on the man, whoever carries this stone with him will abound in all things, and will be shrewd and prudent.

units.la: Viri stantis supra draconem, qui in manu teneat gladium, figuram, si in hæmatithe scul-ptā inuenies, pone in annulo plumbeo, vel ferreo, reo,& obedient ei omnes spiritus subterranei, & reuelabunt ei omnes thesauros leui carmine, nec non extrahendi modum ipsi ostendet.
units.tr: If you find the figure of a man standing on a dragon, holding a sword in his hand, carved in haematite, place it in a ring of lead or iron, and all the subterranean spirits will obey him, and they will reveal to him all the treasures by a light charm; and they will also show him the way of extracting them.

units.la: Viri stantis & habentis loricam indutam, & in capite galeam, in manu vero gladium evaginatum, figuram, si in aliquo lapide sculptam inuenies, & in annulo ferreo tanti ponderis ligaueris, ferenti hunc in prælio nemo resistere poterit.
units.tr: If you find, carved in some stone, the figure of a man standing, wearing a coat of mail and a helmet on his head, and holding a drawn sword in his hand, and if you set it in an iron ring of such weight, no one will be able to resist the one who bears it in battle.

units.la: Viri barbati habentis longum vultum, & curuata supercilia, sedentis super aratrum inter duos tauros, figuram, si sculptam in aliquo lapide inueneris, ad plantationes & ad omnem culturam valet, ad inueniendos thesauros, & bellandum, conuertet inimicos in amicos, & in multis infirmitatibus valet, & siquis eam portauerit, fugient serpentes à facie eius: epilepticos quoque sanat, & si infans eum portauerit ad collum, timorem ab eo expellit, & vexatione malorum spirituum, & si æger portabit, sanitatem recipiet, vtq; maiorem virtutem habeat, debet poni in annulo ferreo, in duplici pondere ad lapidem.
units.tr: A figure of a bearded man with a long face and curved eyebrows, sitting on a plough between two bulls, if you find it carved in some stone, is good for planting and for every kind of cultivation, for finding treasures and for warfare. It turns enemies into friends and is effective in many illnesses. Whoever carries it will see serpents flee from his face. It also cures epileptics. If an infant wears it at the neck, it drives fear away from him and protects him from the vexation of evil spirits. If a sick man carries it, he will recover his health. So that it may have greater power, it should be set in an iron ring with a double weight relative to the stone.

units.la: Aquilæ stantis figura, si in Æthite sculpta & in annulo plumbeo posita fuerit, ferentem reddit acceptum & amatum ab hominibus, & animalia obedient ei.
units.tr: The figure of a standing eagle, if it is carved in aethites and set in a lead ring, makes the wearer acceptable and loved by men, and animals will obey him.

units.la: Arietis & simul Leonis figuram si in aliquo pretiosorum lapidum sculptam inuenies, in argenteo annulo ligaueris, si cum eo discor-des tetigeris, concordabunt.
units.tr: If you find a figure of a Ram and a Lion together carved in some precious stone, bind it in a silver ring. If you touch discordant persons with it, they will agree.

units.la: Capricorni signum sculptum in Cornelio, aut in alio lapide, in annulo argenteo liga, & tecum porta, nec enim personaliter, nec oraliter ab inimicis laederis, nec iudex contra iniustam sententiam dicet, in negotiatione & honore abundabis, & amicitiâ multorum acquires, & omnes fascinationes, quæ contra te facte fuerint, destruentur, in prælio quoq; nullus inimicus, quam etiam fortis fuerit, tibi resistere poterit. Hæc Chael.
units.tr: Engrave the sign of Capricorn on a carnelian or another stone, bind it in a silver ring, and carry it with you. Then you will not be harmed by enemies, either in person or by their words, and no judge will pronounce an unjust sentence against you. You will abound in trade and honour, win the friendship of many, and every enchantment made against you will be destroyed. In battle, too, no enemy, however strong, will be able to resist you. Thus Chael.

units.la: SIGILLA SEV IMAGINES Hermetis.
units.tr: SEALS OR IMAGES OF HERMES.

units.la: HErmes libro quadripart. 14. has commemorat imagines. Hominis imago sculpta in diadocho, stantis, & magnæ staturæ, tenentis in manu dextra obolum, & in alia serpentem, sitque super caput hominis figura Solis, & prostratum teneat sub pedibus Leonem, si posita fuerit in annulo plumbeo cum modico ari hemisiæ ac radice fænugræci, tecum que habueris in ripa fluuij & vocaueris aquaticos spiritus, ab eis de quæsitis responsa accipies.
units.tr: Hermes, in the Quadripartitum, chapter 14, mentions these images. An image of a man, carved on a diadochus stone, standing and of great stature, holding an obol in his right hand and a serpent in the other, with a figure of the Sun above the man's head and a lion lying prostrate beneath his feet. If it is set in a leaden ring with a little half-as of copper and a root of fenugreek, and you carry it with you on a riverbank while calling upon the water spirits, you will receive answers to your questions from them.

units.la: Hominis figura stantis ac tenentis fasciculum herbæ collo appensum cum grossitie renum & num & amplitudine spatularum, si in viridi Iaspide sculpta erit, scias ipsam auxilium præbere febricitantibus, & à febre liberare, & si quis artem medicinæ exercet secumq; portauerit, in discernendis ægritudinibus & cognoscendis medicinis & herbis, in dandisque potionibus maximam gratiam præbet, inq; omni hæmorrhagia & fluxu sanguinis juuat, protinusq; eum compescit.
units.tr: The figure of a man standing and holding a bundle of herbs hung at his neck, with the thickness of the kidneys and the breadth of the shoulder blades, if carved in green jasper, will give help to those with fever and free them from it. If someone who practises medicine carries it with him, it gives him great favour in distinguishing diseases, recognising medicines and herbs, and giving potions. It helps in every haemorrhage and flow of blood, and at once restrains it.

units.la: Turturis marini imago si in lapide marino sculpta sit, & in annulo plumbeo ligata feratur, non poterit lædi ab aliquo, & à senioribus & dominis terrarum diligetur.
units.tr: An image of a sea turtle, if carved in sea stone and carried in a lead ring, cannot be harmed by anyone, and will be loved by elders and lords of lands.

units.la: Aquarij figura si sculpta fuerit in viridi Iaspide, & quis secum portauerit, lucrum præbet in vendendis & emendis rebus, & ab eo mercatores consilium quærent, & in suum domicilium merces portabunt. Auis quæ in ore folium tenet, & in eius conspectu sit caput hominis aspicientis ipsam auem, si in lapide Pangone sculpta sit, eamq; in auro ligaueris, & tecum portaueris, diues eris, & locuples, & ab omnibus venerabilis.
units.tr: The figure of Aquarius, if carved in green jasper and carried by someone, brings profit in buying and selling goods; merchants will seek his counsel and carry their wares to his house. A bird holding a leaf in its mouth, with a human head looking at the bird before it, if carved in pangonus stone and set in gold, and carried with you, will make you rich, wealthy and respected by all.

units.la: Iouis figura, quæ est hominis sedentis super cathedram quadrupedem, sin q; ibi quatuor homines stantes ante Iouem, sintq; manus Iouis erectæ cœlum versus, & in capite habeat diadema, si in Hiacyntho sculpta erit, ac in auro ligata, & quis talem annulum secum portauerit, tauerit, seu figuram huius annuli impressam in cera collo suspendat, à regibus & sapientibus quicquid voluerit, impetrabit.
units.tr: The figure of Jupiter: a man seated on a four-legged chair, with four men standing before Jupiter, Jupiter's hands raised towards heaven, and a diadem on his head. If it is carved in hyacinth and set in gold, and whoever carries such a ring with him, or wears it, or hangs an impression of this ring's figure in wax around his neck, he will obtain from kings and wise men whatever he wishes.

units.la: Hominis imago habentis vultum Leonis & pedes aquilæ, & sub pedibus eius sit draco, & cauda sit extensa, in manu vero ipsius hominis sit baculus, cum quo percutiat caput draconis, si in crystallo sculpta erit, aut in aliquo preciosó lapide, & ligata sit in orichalco, & sub lapide sit moschus & ambra, si quis fert secum talem lapidem, habebit spiritus obedientes, ac magnas facultates accumulabit.
units.tr: The image of a man with the face of a lion and the feet of an eagle, with a dragon under his feet, its tail extended, and in the man's hand a staff with which he strikes the dragon's head; if carved in crystal or some precious stone and set in orichalc, with musk and ambergra beneath the stone, whoever carries such a stone will have obedient spirits and will gather great powers.

units.la: Hominis sedentis supra aquilam, ac in manu virgam tenentis imago, si in crystallo sculpta fuerit, & in annulo æreo, seu cupreo ligata: si quis hunc annulum in die Solis ante exortum ipsius aspexerit, omnes inimicos suos vincet, & superabit, si in die Iouis aspexerit victor belli erit, libenterque omnes homines ei obedient, sed oportet gestantem vestiri albis vestibus, & à Columbina carne abstinere.
units.tr: The image of a man seated on an eagle and holding a rod, if carved in crystal and set in a bronze or copper ring: if anyone looks at this ring on Sunday before sunrise, he will conquer and overcome all his enemies; if he looks at it on Thursday, he will be victor in war, and all men will gladly obey him. But the wearer must dress in white garments and abstain from dove's flesh.

units.la: Hominis figura equitantis, ac tenentis in vna manu frenum, & in alia arcum tensum, & habentis gladium cinctum, si in pyrite lapide sculpta fuerit, & in annulo aureo ligata, & quis secum portauerit, eum victorem reddet in præliis, nec quis ei resistere poterit.
units.tr: The figure of a man riding a horse, holding a bridle in one hand and a drawn bow in the other, and girded with a sword, if carved in pyrite and set in a gold ring: whoever carries it will make him victor in battles, and no one will be able to resist him.

units.la: Mulieris imago habentis crines sparsos, sin[?]p mammammillas, & in eius conspectu fit vir quasi aduenicns, facienfq; ei aliquod amoris signû, si in Hyacintho seu crystallo sculpta fuerit, ac in auro ligata,& sub lapide sit ambra, aloes & artemisia, ferenti hunc lapidem in annulo omnes obedient,& si mulierem cum eo tetigeris,amabit te, & si capiti supposueris, cũ vadis dormitum,quicquid volueris, videbis.
units.tr: The image of a woman with dishevelled hair and bare breasts, with a man before her who seems to be arriving and is making some sign of love to her. If carved in hyacinth or crystal and set in gold, with ambergris, aloes and artemisia beneath the stone, all will obey the one who wears this stone in a ring. If you touch a woman with it, she will love you; and if you place it under your head when you go to sleep, you will see whatever you wish.

units.la: Hominis imago sedentis supra piscem, & super caput hominis sit pauo, si in lapide sculpta sit rubeo, & ipsum sub tabulam in conuiuio posueris, nemo comedens cum dextra,satiabitur.
units.tr: The image of a man sitting on a fish, with a peacock above the man's head. If it is carved in red stone and you place it under the table at a banquet, no one who eats with his right hand will go unsatisfied.

units.la: Hominis nudi stantis figura, & à dextra eius sit puella stans, cuius capilli sint ligati circa caput, & vir teneat dextram suam supra collum puellæ & sinistram supra pectus, aspiciatque vultum eius; ipsa vero in terram, si in aliquo lapide sculpta erit, ac in ferreo ligata annulo, & sub lapide sit parum linguæ passeris, vpupæ, myrrhæ, aluminis, sanguinisque hominis, qui hunc annulum portauerit, inuictus erit, nec vllus poterit ei resistere, nec fera aliqua ei nocebit. Epilepticis quoque valet, si ceram rubeam signaueris cum eo, & si ad collum canis ponatur, latrare non permittit.
units.tr: The figure of a naked man standing, with a standing girl at his right whose hair is bound around her head. The man rests his right hand on the girl's neck and his left on her breast, and looks at her face, while she looks down at the ground. If this is carved in some stone and set in an iron ring, with a little of a sparrow's tongue, hoopoe, myrrh, alum and human blood beneath the stone, the one who wears this ring will be invincible; no one will be able to resist him, and no wild beast will harm him. It is also good for epileptics, if you seal red wax with it; and if it is placed at a dog's neck, it will not let the dog bark.

units.la: Hominis imago tenentis in manu flores, si in Cornelio sculpta erit,ac in annulo stanneo posita, & annulus fabricatus fuerit die Lunæ aut Veneris, 4. 8. aut 12. hora, tange quem voluer-is hoc annulo, & obediet tibi.
units.tr: The image of a man holding flowers in his hand, if carved in cornelian and set in a tin ring, and the ring is made on a Monday or Friday at the fourth, eighth or twelfth hour: touch whomever you wish with this ring, and he will obey you.

units.la: Hominis barbati figuram habentis vultum longum, superciliaque curua, sedentis super aratrum inter duos tauros, habentisque vultu-rem in manu, in lapide sculptam, scias virtutem habere in plantatione arborum, & inuentione thesaurorum, ac victorem in prælio efficere, serpentes à facie gestantis fugandi: epilepticos sanat, omnemq; vexationem malorum spirituum tollit, debet autem in annulo ferreo ligari, & gestari.
units.tr: The figure of a bearded man with a long face and curved eyebrows, sitting on a plough between two bulls and holding a vulture in his hand, carved in stone: know that it has power in planting trees and finding treasures, and makes the wearer victor in battle, and puts serpents to flight from his face. It cures epileptics and removes every vexation of evil spirits. It should be bound in an iron ring and worn.

units.la: Hominis tenentis falcem in manu super caput suum, figura, & sub pedibus crocodilum, si in lapide sculpta erit, ac in annulo plumbeo ligata, & sub lapide sit parum radicis squillæ, qui secum hunc annulum portauerit, ab inimicis securus erit, & in itinere à latronibus.
units.tr: The figure of a man holding a sickle in his hand above his head, with a crocodile under his feet, if carved in stone and set in a lead ring, with a little root of squill beneath the stone: whoever carries this ring with him will be safe from enemies, and on a journey from robbers.

units.la: Hominis figura tenentis gladiũ in manu, & sedentis supra draconem, si in Amethysto sculpta fuerit, ac in plumbeo annulo, vel ferreo ligata, & in digito feratur, spiritus obedient, reuelabuntq; ei qualescunq; thesauros.
units.tr: The figure of a man holding a sword in his hand and seated on a dragon, if carved in amethyst and set in a lead or iron ring and worn on the finger, the spirits will obey, and they will reveal to him whatever treasures there are.

units.la: Aquilæ stantis figura si in Æthite lapide sculpta fuerit, & in annulo plumbeo ligata, virtutem habet, qui secum portauerit capiendi multos pisces, nec vlla fera ei nocebit, atque hominibus diligetur.
units.tr: If the figure of a standing eagle is carved on an aethites stone and set in a leaden ring, whoever carries it with him has the power of catching many fish, no wild beast will harm him, and he will be loved by men.

units.la: Hominis habentis in manu palmam figura, si in aliquo lapide sculpta erit, reddit gestantem gratum, & amabilem potentibus & principibus. Hæc ex Hermete.
units.tr: A figure of a man holding a palm in his hand, if it is carved on some stone, makes the wearer pleasing and lovable to the powerful and to princes. These things are from Hermes.

units.la: IMAGINES SEV SIGILLA Thetelis.
units.tr: IMAGES OR SEALS OF Thetel.

units.la: THetel vetustissimus Doctor tractans de sculpturis lapidum, ait, has sculpturas in conuenientibus lapidibus repertas, maximam habere virtutem.
units.tr: Thetel, a very ancient teacher, treating of carvings on stones, says that these carvings, when found on suitable stones, have very great power.

units.la: Hominis imago sculpta in Iaspide habentis scutum in sinistra, & in dextra idolum, vel aliquid bellicosum, & loco pedum sint viperæ & loco capitis hominis sit caput Galli vel Leonis, virtutem habet contra inimicos, & victorem gestantem reddit, valetque aduersus venena, sanguinem quoque stringit à quacunque parte fluat.
units.tr: An image of a man carved in jasper, holding a shield in the left hand and in the right an idol or some warlike thing, with vipers in place of feet and the head of a man replaced by the head of a cock or a lion, has power against enemies and makes the wearer victorious; it is also effective against poisons, and it staunches blood from whatever part it flows.

units.la: Hominis figura habentis fasciculum herbæ in collo, si in Iaspide sculpta fuerit, virtutem habet discernendi, seu cognoscendi infirmitates, sanguinemque à quocunque loco fluat, frenat, dicuntque hunc lapidem habuisse Galenum.
units.tr: A figure of a man with a bundle of herbs at the neck, if carved in jasper, has the power of discerning or recognising infirmities, and it restrains blood from whatever place it flows; and they say that Galen had this stone.

units.la: Crucem sculptam in Iaspide viridi, dicunt habere potentiam liberandi gestantem ab aquæ submersione. Fœmina habens in vna manu auem & in altera pisce m: si sculpta fuerit in Chrysolito, ad negociandum multum valet.
units.tr: A cross carved in green jasper is said to have the power of freeing the wearer from drowning in water. A woman holding a bird in one hand and a fish in the other, if carved in chrysolite, is of great value for trade.

units.la: Lupi figura sculpta in Iaspide contra astu-tiam valet, & insana verba prohibet pro-ferre.
units.tr: A figure of a wolf carved in jasper is effective against cunning and prevents the utterance of mad words.

units.la: Cerui figura in Iaspide sculpta virtutem ha-bet sanandi & liberandi lunaticos & phre-neticos,
units.tr: A figure of a stag carved in jasper has the power of healing and freeing lunatics and frenetics.

units.la: Imperatoris figura in Iaspide sculpta cum capite erecto, gestantem reddit amabilem ab omni creatura, & quicquid petierit, ob-tinebit.
units.tr: A figure of an emperor carved in jasper, with head erect, makes the wearer beloved by every creature, and he will obtain whatever he seeks.

units.la: Virginis figura cum veste profusa tenentis in manu laurum, si sculpta fuerit in Iaspide, gestantem efficit securum à submersione a-quæ, necà Dæmone vexabitur, facitq; poten-tem, & omnia impetrantem.
units.tr: A figure of a Virgin in a flowing garment, holding a laurel in her hand, if carved in jasper, makes the wearer safe from drowning in water, is not troubled by a demon, and makes him powerful and obtaining all things.

units.la: Hominis figura habens in manu inscriptam palmam, si in Iaspide reperiatur, potentem reddit gestantem principibusq; gratum. Ha-ctenus Thetel.
units.tr: A figure of a man having a palm inscribed on his hand, if found in jasper, makes the wearer powerful and pleasing to princes. So far Thetel.

units.la: SCVLPTVRÆ SALO-monia.
units.tr: Solomon's Sculptures.

units.la: VEtustissimus inuentus est libellus in de-serto apud filios Israelis, qui quoniā in eo multa Salomonis opera repetiebantur, Salomoni fuit ascriptus. Titulus libri erat, de Sigillis lapidum secundum nomen tuum Domine, & secundum cursum stellarum.
units.tr: An very old little book was found in the desert among the sons of Israel. Because it repeated many works of Solomon, it was ascribed to Solomon. Its title was: On the seals of stones according to your name, O Lord, and according to the course of the stars.

units.la: Hominis sedentis super aratrum figura, habentis collum parvum & prolixam barbam, quatuorq; homines iacent in collo ipsius, & teneat in una manu vulpem, in altera vulturem, scias istud sigillum collo appensum ad omnes valere plantationes, omnesq; thesaurorum inventiones: probationem autem istius sic instities, accipe lanam nigram puram sine tinctura, involue lapidem, poneq; inter paleas tritici, & capiti suppone, videbisq; tunc in somno omnes thesauros istius regionis in qua fueris, simulq; habet virtutem sanandi omnes bestiarum languores, si aquam, in qua lotus fuerit, biberint.
units.tr: A figure of a man sitting on a plough, with a short neck and a long beard, with four men lying on his neck, and holding a fox in one hand and a vulture in the other. Know that this seal, hung on the neck, is effective for all plantings and for all discoveries of treasure. Test it thus: take pure black wool, undyed, wrap the stone in it, place it among wheat chaff, and put it under the head. Then in sleep you will see all the treasures of the region where you are. It also has the power to heal all diseases of beasts, if they drink the water in which it has been washed.

units.la: Hominem sculptum in Iaspide viridi, qui habeat clypeum pendente in collo, & supra caput galea cum gladio erecto, pedibusq; calcet serpentem, appone collo, & non timebis vllū inimicum, in omnibus rebus eris victor maxime vero Martialibus, debetq; ligari in aere.
units.tr: A man carved in green jasper, wearing a shield hanging from the neck, a helmet on the head with a drawn sword, and treading on a serpent under the feet. Attach it to the neck, and you will fear no enemy; you will be victorious in all things, especially in martial affairs. It should be bound in bronze.

units.la: Equus gerens in dorso crocodilum in hiacyntho albo sculptus, amabilem facit hominibus & bestiis.
units.tr: A horse carrying a crocodile on its back, carved in white hyacinth, makes a person lovable to men and beasts.

units.la: Hominis sedentis figura & mulieris stantis ante eum, habentis capillos extensos usque ad femur, leuantis v. oculos sursum, si in Cor-nelio sculpta fuerit, scias virtutem eius esse, omnem hominem tam marem vel foeminam reddere obedientem, debetq; in tanto pondere auri ligari, quantum ipse lapis habet, subtus autem pone betonicam & ambram.
units.tr: A figure of a man sitting and a woman standing before him, with hair spread down to the thigh and eyes raised upward, carved in cornelian. Know that its power is to make every man or woman obedient. It should be bound in gold of the same weight as the stone itself, and beneath the stone place betony and ambergris.

units.la: Equum spumantem cum viro supra se tenente sceptrum manu, in amethysto sculptum, scias illud sigillum prodesse ad omnes res quas habet, qui illud gerit, omnesque principes & primates erunt ei obedientes, debet autem ligari in auro vel argento in duplo ad sigillum.
units.tr: A foaming horse with a man above it holding a sceptre in his hand, carved in amethyst. Know that this seal is useful for all the things he has, and that all princes and chief men will be obedient to him who wears it. It should be bound in gold or silver, doubled around the seal.

units.la: Capitis hominis cum longa barba ac modico sanguinis circa collum, si in adamante imago sculpta reperiatur, scias ad victoriam audaciamq; conferre, & corpus ab omni laesione praeseruare, valetq; ad impetrandam gratiam a principibus.
units.tr: The head of a man with a long beard and a little blood about the neck, if an image is found carved in adamant, know that it confers victory and boldness, preserves the body from all injury, and is effective for obtaining favour from princes.

units.la: Hominis volentis instrumentis ludere figura in sapphyro sculpta, gratiosissimum omnibus reddit.
units.tr: A figure of a man playing with instruments, carved in sapphire, makes its bearer most pleasing to all.

units.la: Galli imago, vel trium puellarum si in Achate reperiatur, hominem gratiosum apud Deum & homines reddit.
units.tr: An image of a cock, or of three girls, if found in agate, makes the bearer pleasing to God and men.

units.la: Leonis figura in Granato sculpta diuitias praebet & honores, cor laetificat, tristitiamq; expellit.
units.tr: A figure of a lion carved in garnet bestows riches and honours, gladdens the heart and drives out sadness.

units.la: Cerui aut columbi imago in Onyche sculpta, gestanti praebet animositatem aduersus daemonas. D s Ho-
units.tr: An image of a stag or a dove carved in onyx gives the bearer courage against demons.

units.la: Hominis figura in similitudine mercatoris portantis merces ad vendendum, aut hominis sedentis sub centurione, si in Smaragdo reperiatur; dat divitias, victoremque reddit, & ab angustiis subleuat.
units.tr: A figure of a man in the likeness of a merchant carrying wares for sale, or of a man sitting under a centurion, if found in emerald, gives riches, makes the bearer victorious, and relieves him from distress.

units.la: Tauri vel vituli imago in magnete reperta, portanti felicia praebet itinera per omnia loca, valetq; contra omnes incantationes.
units.tr: An image of a bull or calf found in magnetite gives the bearer fortunate journeys through all places, and is effective against all incantations.

units.la: Equi aut lupi figura in Iaspide reperta febres fugat, sanguinemq; sistit.
units.tr: A figure of a horse or wolf found in jasper drives away fevers and stops bleeding.

units.la: Hominis figura coronati in Topatio gestantem efficit bonum, morigeratum dilectumque Deo & hominib. praebetq; honores ac dignitates.
units.tr: A figure of a crowned man in topaz makes the bearer good, well-mannered, and beloved of God and men, and brings him honours and dignities.

units.la: Hominis armati cum ense in manu, si in Sardio vel Amethysto sculpta reperiatur imago, gerentem acquirere facit perfectam & bonam memoriam, redditq; prudentem.
units.tr: A figure of an armed man with a sword in his hand, if an image is found carved in sard or amethyst, makes the bearer acquire a perfect and good memory, and makes him prudent.

units.la: Cerui vel hirci figura in Chalcedonio reperta sculpta, virtutem dat augendi divitias, si in capsula pecuniaria reseruetur.
units.tr: A figure of a stag or he-goat found carved in chalcedony gives the power of increasing riches, if it is kept in a money-box.

units.la: Leporis imago in Iaspide portantem a nullo daemone laedi patitur,
units.tr: An image of a hare in jasper keeps the bearer from being harmed by any demon.

units.la: Locusta marina in berillo sculpta, rixas conciliat, & matrimonium in amore coniungit.
units.tr: A sea locust carved in beryl settles quarrels and joins a marriage in love.

units.la: Nocticoracis figura, quia Palladis auis est, sculpta in lapide qui facit ad scientiam, hominem facit scientissimum & eloquentem.
units.tr: A figure of a night-raven, because it is the bird of Pallas, carved in a stone that is suited to knowledge, makes the man most learned and eloquent.

units.la: Pauonis imago sculpta in conueniente lapide gestantes reddit diuites. Ho-
units.tr: An image of a peacock carved in a suitable stone makes its bearer rich.

units.la: Hominis figura interficientis Leonem aut aliam bestiam cum gladio, gestantem asturum, victoriosum & amabilem reddit.
units.tr: A figure of a man killing a lion or another beast with a sword, carried by one who wears a hawk, makes him victorious and lovable.

units.la: Hominis tenentis laurum vel palmam in manu dextra imago, portantem efficit causarum & praeliorum victorem, amabilem & potentem in regione sua.
units.tr: An image of a man holding a laurel or palm in the right hand makes the bearer victor in lawsuits and battles, lovable and powerful in his own region.

units.la: Hominis alati figura habentis sub pedibus serpentem ac tenentis caput eius in manibus, gestantem diuitem, prudentem & amabilem reddit omnibus.
units.tr: A figure of a winged man with a serpent under his feet and holding its head in his hands makes the bearer rich, prudent and lovable to all.

units.la: Formicae habentis spicam vel granum in aliquo lapide sculpta imago, ad diuitias valet acquirendas.
units.tr: An image of an ant holding an ear of grain or a seed, carved in some stone, is effective for acquiring riches.

units.la: Galli figura tenentis rostro coronam vel Zonam, in duello victoriam dabit, praesertim si in gallinaceo fuerit.
units.tr: A figure of a cock holding a crown or girdle in its beak will give victory in a duel, especially if it is carved in a cockle-stone.

units.la: Hominis stantis, cuius caput sit bouis, pedes vero aquilae figura, in gemma aliqua sculptam si inueneris, inquit ceram impresseris, nullus hominum de te male loquetur.
units.tr: If you find a figure of a standing man, whose head is an ox's and whose feet are an eagle's, carved in some gem, and you press it into wax, no one will speak evil of you.

units.la: Basiliscum & draconem inter se pugnantes si in Cornelio inueneris sculptos, sitque ibi caput bouis, bellaturus applica collo, omnesque bestias vinces tam marinas quam terrestres.
units.tr: If you find a basilisk and a dragon fighting one another carved in cornelian, with an ox's head there, apply it to the neck when you are about to fight, and you will conquer all beasts, both sea and land.

units.la: Hominis nudi inflati & coronati, tenentis in vna manu scyphum, in altera ramum herbae, figura in Gagate sculpta, ligataque in annulo cuiuscuiusuis metalli, gestantem protinus a febre liberat.
units.tr: A figure of a naked, puffed-up and crowned man, holding a cup in one hand and a branch of herb in the other, carved in jet and set in a ring of any metal, immediately frees the bearer from fever.

units.la: Viri sedentis super piscę figura in Iaspide rubeo sculpta, pannoq; alicuius impositā, conuiuantem si cum dextra comederit, non saturari faciet.
units.tr: A figure of a man sitting on a fish, carved in red jasper and placed on some cloth: if he eats with his right hand while feasting, he will not be satisfied.

units.la: Mulieris figuram habentis crines sparsos, vel mammillas nudas, inq; conspectu eius sit vir cernēs eius faciem, si in hiacyntho, granato vel crystallo inueneris sculptam, ligauerisq; in annulo aureo, tanti ponderis vt lapis est, sub verò lapide sit ambra, aloes, polypodium, gestantem efficiet omnibus amicabilem, siq; supponatur capiti, in somno videbit, quæcunque voluerit.
units.tr: A figure of a woman with dishevelled hair or bare breasts, with a man before her looking into her face, if you find it carved in hyacinth, garnet or crystal, and bind it in a gold ring of the same weight as the stone, with ambergris, aloes and polypody under the stone, will make the bearer friendly to all. And if it is placed under the head, he will see in sleep whatever he wishes.

units.la: Viri equitantis & tenentis in manu frenum, & in alia arcum cum gladio cincto, figuram si in pyrite sculptam inuenies, ligeturque in annulo aureo, gestantem victorem reddit in prælio cui nemo resistere poterit, & si quis huc annulum submerserit in oleo muschato, omnes ipsum pertimescent, si inunxerit vultum suum illo oleo, nec ei poterunt se opponere.
