units.tr: A figure of a man on horseback holding a bridle in one hand and a bow in the other, with a sword girt on, if you find it carved in pyrite and set in a gold ring, makes the bearer a victor in battle whom no one can resist. And if someone dips this ring in musk oil, all will fear him; if he anoints his face with that oil, no one will be able to oppose him.

units.la: Viri stantis qui sit nudus, & a dextris eius sit puella nuda stans, eiusque capilli sint ligati circa caput, figuram, si in magnete sculptam inuenies, & vir tencat dextram suam super collo puellæ, sinistram vero supra pectus, & vir aspiciat vultum puellæ, hæc autem terram, pone in anannulo ferreo tanti ponderis quanti est lapis, includeq; sub annulo vpupæ linguam, myrrhā, alumen, & de sanguine hominis, quantum linguæ pondus est, ferenti hunc annulum, nullus inimicus poterit resistere in conspectu eius, sive in bello, sive alibi, nec latro, nec fera nocens poterit intrare domum in qua hic lapis repositus fuerit, & si epilepticus aquam biberit in qua lotus fuerit, sanabitur; Cera quoque rubea si eo signetur colloque canis fuerit appensa, latrare eum prohibebit.
units.tr: A figure of a standing man who is naked, with a naked girl standing at his right side, her hair tied about her head, if you find it carved in magnetite, and the man lays his right hand on the girl's neck and his left on her breast, and the man looks at the girl's face, and it is earth: set it in an iron ring of the same weight as the stone, and enclose under the ring the tongue of a hoopoe, myrrh, alum, and blood from a man, as much as the weight of the tongue. To the one who wears this ring no enemy will be able to resist before him, whether in war or elsewhere; no thief, nor any harmful beast, will be able to enter the house in which this stone is kept. And if an epileptic drinks water in which it has been washed, he will be cured. Red wax also, if sealed with it and hung on a dog's neck, will keep him from barking.

units.la: Militem super equo currentem cum cornu ad collum, &cum arbore ante ipsum, sculptum in pretioso aliquo lapide, scias valere ad omnes venationes.
units.tr: A soldier riding a horse at full gallop with a horn at his neck, and a tree before him, carved in some precious stone: know that it is effective for all hunting.

units.la: Fœminam tenentem in vna manu auem, in altera piscem, in crystallo sculptam, scias valere ad capiendum aues, debetque ligari in argento.
units.tr: A woman holding a bird in one hand and a fish in the other, carved in crystal: know that it is effective for catching birds, and it should be bound in silver.

units.la: Hominis figuram cum hircino capite loco sui, scias valere ad acquirendum diuitias.
units.tr: A figure of a man with a goat's head in place of his own: know that it is effective for acquiring riches.

units.la: Aquilæ figura in crystallo sculpta gestantem reddit diuitem, victoriosum & eloquentem.
units.tr: A figure of an eagle carved in crystal makes the bearer rich, victorious and eloquent.

units.la: Cornutum animal, quod equum subtus se ferat, & equus retro se ducat medietatem capræ, sculptum pretiosiore aliquo lapide, scias plurimum valere ad domandum quamcunq; bestiam, debetq; ligari in annulo plumbeo.
units.tr: A horned animal which carries a horse beneath itself, and a horse which draws half a goat behind itself, carved in some precious stone: know that it is very effective for taming any beast, and it should be bound in a lead ring.

units.la: Turturis figuram si in Pangone inueneris sculptam & in annulo plumbeo, ferens nunquam vulnerabitur, nec malum accipiet, sed honorabitur ab omnibus, maximè à Seniori-bus.
units.tr: If you find a figure of a turtle-dove carved on a pangonus stone and set in a leaden ring, the wearer will never be wounded or suffer harm, and he will be honoured by all, especially by the elders.

units.la: Auis tenentis folium in ore, sitque in ore & conspectu eius caput hominis aut vulturis, figuram, si in auro sculptam inueneris, ferens ex omnibus quæ emturus est & venditurus lucrum acquiret, àque emptoribus inuestigabi-tur.
units.tr: If you find carved in gold the figure of a bird holding a leaf in its mouth, with the head of a man or a vulture in its mouth and before its eyes, the wearer will gain profit from everything he is about to buy or sell, and buyers will seek him out.

units.la: Leonis vel draconis vultus habenris duo capita cum cauda delicata, vel viri in cuius dextra sit baculus,& percutiat caput Leonis, figuram, si in crystallo sculptam inuenKris, posuerisque in orichalco, sub vero lapide moschum & ambram, tecumq; portaueris, omnes tibi obedi-ent, facultatemq; tuam amplificabis, signata cum eo cera eamdem habebit virtutem.
units.tr: A figure with the face of a lion or dragon, with two heads and a delicate tail, or of a man with a staff in his right hand striking the lion's head, carved on crystal and set in orichalcum, with musk and ambergris beneath the stone: if you carry it, all will obey you and your wealth will increase. Wax sealed with it will have the same power.

units.la: Equi alati, qui Pegasus dicitur, figura, si in a-liquo lapide sculpto inuenitur, conducit mili-tantibus, & in campestri bello dat audaciam & alacritatem.
units.tr: The figure of the winged horse called Pegasus, if found carved on some stone, brings success to soldiers and gives boldness and eagerness in a battle on the open field.

units.la: Viri & serpentis circumdantis visum figu-ram, si in aliquo lapide sculptam inuenies, ge-renti scias præbere victoriam in prælio campe-stri.
units.tr: A figure of a man with a serpent coiled about him, if you find it carved on some stone, is known to give victory in a pitched battle to the one who wears it.

units.la: Arboris, vel vitis, vel spicæ figura in aliquo lapide sculpta gestantem facit in victu & ami-tia. [illegible, ~2 letters] étu abundare, principesque reddit benevolos.
units.tr: A figure of a tree, a vine or an ear of grain, carved on some stone, makes the wearer abound in livelihood and friendship [illegible], and renders princes well disposed towards him.

units.la: Mars armatus vel virgo stolata cum circumflexa veste tenens in manu laurum, in Iaspide si inueniatur, potentem gestantem reddit ad arma perficienda, & à morte violenta, aquæque submersione liberat, casibusque aduersis.
units.tr: Mars armed, or a robed maiden with a flowing garment holding a laurel in her hand, if found on jasper, makes the wearer powerful in carrying out his undertakings, and frees him from violent death, from drowning and from adverse chances.

units.la: Hominis armati in equo cum lancea figura in amethysto sculpta facit gestantem victoriosum in campestri bello.
units.tr: The figure of an armed man on horseback with a lance, carved on amethyst, makes the wearer victorious in a battle on the open field.

units.la: Herculis figuram, tenentis in dextra clauam, interficientis Leonem vel aliud monstrum, si in lapide sculptam reperies, scias præbere victoriam in campestri pugna.
units.tr: If you find a carved stone showing Hercules holding a club in his right hand and killing a lion or some other monster, know that it gives victory in a battle on the open field.

units.la: Iouis figura, quæ sit in forma hominis cum arietis capite, gestantem facit amabilem, citoque impetrantem quicquid voluerit.
units.tr: The figure of Jupiter, in the form of a man with a ram's head, makes the wearer pleasing and quickly obtains whatever he wishes.

units.la: Virgo aut puella cum Lampade in cry-stallo sculpta, virtutem habet custodiendi oculorum lumen.
units.tr: A maiden or girl with a lamp, carved on crystal, has the power of guarding the light of the eyes.

units.la: Igneæ triplicitatis, id est, arietis, Leonis & Sagittarii figura sculpta in lapide pretioso, omnibus frigidis ægritudinibus valere perhibetur, opitulariq; febribus phlegmaticis, & ob Planetarum, qui in illis signis tenent dominium, dignitatem, reddere Deo & hominibus gratū, facundum, ingeniosum, honorumque & dignitatum facile potiri valentem: debet autem tem ita sculpi, vt in triangulo Leo teneat conum, aries in basi dextram, Sagittarius sinistram.
units.tr: The figure of the fiery triplicity, that is, of Aries, Leo and Sagittarius, carved on a precious stone, is said to be good for all cold diseases and to help phlegmatic fevers. Because of the dignity of the planets that hold rule in those signs, it makes the wearer pleasing to God and men, eloquent and clever, and easily able to attain honours and offices. It should be carved so that in the triangle Leo holds a cone, Aries holds the right side of the base, and Sagittarius the left.

units.la: Terreae triplicitatis, id est tauri, virginis & Capricorni imago lapidi insculpta, omnibus calidis & humidis ægritudinibus auxilium præstabit, gestantemq; inclinabit ad opera ruralia, vt sunt arare, plantare, seminare, vineas excolere & similia, debet autem in Cono esse Capricornus, in basis dextra taurus, in sinistra virgo.
units.tr: The image of the earthy triplicity, that is, of Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn, engraved on a stone, will give help against all hot and moist diseases, and it will incline the wearer to rural labours, such as ploughing, planting, sowing, tending vineyards and the like. It should be arranged so that Capricorn is on the cone, Taurus on the right of the base, and Virgo on the left.

units.la: Aeriæ triplicitatis, id est, geminorum, libræ & aquarii imago, in lapide sculpta, ab omnibus ægritudinibus frigidis & siccis ex humore melancholico oriundis, liberat, præsertim vero quartana, eritq; in trianguli cuspide libra, in basis dextra aquarius, in sinistra gemini.
units.tr: The image of the airy triplicity, that is, of Gemini, Libra and Aquarius, carved in stone, frees from all cold and dry diseases arising from melancholic humour, and especially from quartan fever. Libra should be on the point of the triangle, Aquarius on the right of the base, and Gemini on the left.

units.la: Aquae triplicitatis, id est Cancri, Scorpii, piscium figura lapidi insculpta, à calidis & siccis morbis liberat, vt Ethica, omnibusq; cholerae morbis, verùm gestantem reddit inconstantem, iniustum & veritatis osorem, debet autem in coronide trianguli esse Cancer, in basis dextra Pisces, in sinistra Mars.
units.tr: The figure of the watery triplicity, that is, of Cancer, Scorpio and the Fishes, engraved on a stone, frees from hot and dry diseases, like the ethical ones, and from all diseases of choler. But it makes the wearer inconstant, unjust and a hater of truth. It should be arranged so that Cancer is on the crown of the triangle, the Fishes on the right of the base, and Mars on the left.

units.la: Saturni figura insculpta lapidibus est eiusmodi. Vir senex falcem tenens in manu, habens barbam non multum pilosam: hæc figura sculpta in lapide de natura Saturni gestantem reddit potentem cum continua potestatis augmentatione.
units.tr: The figure of Saturn carved on stones is of this kind: an old man holding a sickle in his hand, with a not very bushy beard. This figure, carved in a stone of Saturn's nature, makes the wearer powerful, with a continual increase of authority.

units.la: Iovis Imago est hominis sedentis in solio seu in quadrupede cathedra, virgam tenentis vna, altera vero pilam; seu tenentis idolum, Cancrum vel piscem, & ante pedes habentis aquilam: Sed apud Magiæ Doctores aliter figuratur, hominis enim figuram sculpunt cum arietino capite, rugosis calcaneis, subtili pectore, quæ si lapidi, maximè Krabati insculpatur, gestantem reddit fortunatum, amabilem religiosisq; gratum, extollitq; ad honores & dignitates.
units.tr: The image of Jupiter is of a man sitting on a throne, or on a four-legged chair, holding a rod in one hand and a ball in the other; or holding an idol, a crab or a fish, with an eagle before his feet. But among the teachers of magic it is depicted differently: they carve the figure of a man with a ram's head, wrinkled heels and a slender chest. If this is engraved on a stone, especially on a bloodstone, it makes the wearer fortunate, lovable and pleasing to the devout, and raises him to honours and dignities.

units.la: Martis imago multipliciter in lapide figuratur, interdum cum vexillo in manu, interdum cum lancea, aut alio instrumento bellico, semper tamen armatus, & aliquando equester: huius lapidis sic sculpti virtus gestantem reddit victoriosum, audacem, bellicosum, maximè vero si sculpatur in lapide virtutis consimilis.
units.tr: The image of Mars is depicted in many ways on stone: sometimes with a banner in his hand, sometimes with a lance or another military instrument, but always armed, and sometimes on horseback. The power of a stone so carved makes the wearer victorious, bold and warlike, especially if it is carved on a stone of similar virtue.

units.la: Solis figura diversimodè reperitur, interdum instar ⊙ cum radiis circumquaq; : aliquando instar hominis sedentis in solio cum capillis sparsis, & veste profusa, nec non in curru, ac si ab equis quadrigis veheretur, ita ut circumcirca currum sint 12. Zodiaci signa: Virtus autem huius figurae in aliquo lapide sculptae gestantem reddit imperantem, Magnatibusque gratum.
units.tr: The figure of the Sun is found in various forms: sometimes like ⊙ with rays all round; sometimes like a man sitting on a throne, with his hair loose and his garment flowing, and also in a chariot, as if carried by four horses, with the twelve signs of the zodiac all around the chariot. The virtue of this figure carved on some stone makes the wearer a ruler and pleasing to the great.

units.la: Veneris imagines similiter multae sunt, lapidibus tamen sequens frequentius insculpitur: Mulier cum magna veste & stola, manuq; tenens laurum: huius virtus est agilitatem dare in rebus agendis, omniaq; ad optatum finem deducere, timorem submersionis aquaticæ auferre, honores verò muliebres afferre.
units.tr: There are likewise many images of Venus, but the following is engraved on stones most often: a woman with a large robe and a stole, holding a laurel in her hand. Its virtue is to give quickness in doing things, to bring all things to the desired end, to remove the fear of drowning, and to bring honours fitting for a woman.

units.la: Mercurii figura homo est gracilis pectoris, pulcram habens barbam cum talaribus, caduceam tenens virgam cum gallo ante pedes, aut cum serpente sub pedibus: virtus eius est conferre ad scientiam & oratoriam comparandam, mercatoribus locupletandis quoq; maximum præstat auxilium.
units.tr: The figure of Mercury is a slender man with a narrow chest, a fine beard, winged sandals, carrying a herald's staff, with a cock before his feet or a serpent under them. Its virtue is to contribute to acquiring learning and oratory, and it gives the greatest help in enriching merchants.

units.la: Lunæ imagines variæ sunt, aliquando enim figuratur in propria Lunæ figura, cum cornibus, interdum in curru, vt puella cum catnibus & pharetra, cum canibus sequentibus ceruum: huius imaginis virtus est præbere expeditionem in legionibus, ex his bona & honores, inq; omnibus rebus agendis præstare celeritatem & facilitatem, adque optatum finem omnia deducere. Verum caute obseruandum, vt etiam supra monitum est, Planetam, cuius imaginem in annulo conueniente sculptam cupis, optimè debere esse dispositum, hoc est, non combustum, retrogradum, malorumque radiis oppressum aut tactum, sed in bono cœli loco, oriente vel Medio Cœli, cum Ioue vel Venere in dignitatibusq; essentialibus, aliâs imago Vana existet, nulliusque momenti.
units.tr: The images of the Moon vary. Sometimes she is depicted in her own form, with horns; sometimes in a chariot, or as a girl with a hunting dress and a quiver, with dogs following a stag. The virtue of this image is to give success in the armies, and from these goods and honours, and to give speed and ease in all undertakings, and to bring all things to the desired end. But one must observe carefully, as was also warned above, that the planet whose image you wish to have carved in a suitable ring must be very well disposed, that is, not burnt, not retrograde, and not oppressed or touched by the rays of malefic planets, but in a good place of the heavens, rising or in the midheaven, with Jupiter or Venus in their essential dignities. Otherwise the image will be vain and of no importance.

units.la: Cæterum Vrsi imaginem sic formarunt veteres:
units.tr: Moreover, the ancients formed the image of the Bear in this way:

units.la: Binas vrsas insculpunt circumuolutas à serpente, Maior vrsa in capite circumflexionis, minor in cauda continetur: quæ imago in aliquo lapide sculpta, gestantem scientem reddit, versutum & potentem.
units.tr: They carve two bears wound about by a serpent: the Greater Bear is contained in the bend of the head, the Lesser in the tail. This image, carved on some stone, makes the wearer knowing and shrewd and powerful.

units.la: Coronæ imago similitudinem coronæ Regiæ cum pluribus habet stellis, interdum similitudine regis capite coronati figuratur, existit in Septentrionali parte & signo Sagittarii, estque de natura Veneris & Mercuri, si hæc imago in lapide fuerit sculpta, dat gestantibus honores & scientiam, regiamq; gratiam.
units.tr: The image of the Crown has the likeness of a royal crown with several stars. Sometimes it is depicted as the likeness of a king with a crowned head. It lies in the northern part and in the sign of Sagittarius, and it is of the nature of Venus and Mercury. If this image is carved on a stone, it gives those who wear it honours, knowledge and royal favour.

units.la: Herculis quoque incuruati imago talis est: Vir in genua prolapsus tenens in manu clauam interficiensque Leonem: aliquando vir cum Leonina pelle in manu, talesque figurae in decente lapide sculptæ ad victoriam conferunt bellicam, maximè si in Achate gestetur.
units.tr: The image of Hercules bent over is also of this kind: a man fallen on his knees, holding a club in his hand and killing a lion; sometimes a man with a lion's skin in his hand. Such figures carved on a suitable stone bring warlike victory, especially if they are worn on an agate.

units.la: Cygni siue gallinæ imago, expansis alis colloque incuruato, gratum gestantem reddit populo, scientem, diuitem, podagramque paralysin & quartanam pellit.
units.tr: The image of the Swan or Hen, with wings spread and neck bent, makes the wearer pleasing to the people, knowing and rich, and it drives away gout, paralysis and quartan fever.

units.la: Cephei figura habentis præcinctum ensem cum brachiis & manibus expansis in lapide sculpta, cautum reddit & scientem, & si puluinari dormientis supponatur, in somnos delectabiles facit apparere.
units.tr: The figure of Cepheus, with a sword girded on, arms and hands outstretched, carved in stone, makes the wearer cautious and knowing. If it is placed under the pillow of a sleeper, it makes pleasant sleeps appear.

units.la: Cassiopeia mulieris imago est sedentis in Cathedra habentis manus porrectas ad modum crucis, aliquando cum triangulo in capite, in signo autem tauri constituitur, & in septentrionali parte, eius natura est de Saturno & Venere: si haec sculpta fuerit in conuenienti lapide, virtus eius erit, hominibus sanitatem praebere, infirma & defatigata corpora restaurare, quietem & tranquillitatem post conceptum laborem gestantibus praebere, amoenum & suauem somnum praestare.
units.tr: The image of Cassiopeia is that of a woman sitting in a chair with her hands stretched out in the form of a cross. Sometimes she has a triangle on her head. She is placed in the sign of Taurus and in the northern part, and her nature is of Saturn and Venus. If this is carved on a suitable stone, its virtue is to give health to men, to restore weak and worn-out bodies, to give rest and tranquillity to those who wear it after toil has been undertaken, and to give a pleasant and sweet sleep.

units.la: Andromeda puellae imago est, habens crines sparsos, ac remissas manus a tauro continetur in septentrione, Venerisque naturae est: eius virtus est si in lapide sculpta erit, rixas & iurgia inter virum & vxorem ortas reconciliare, & stabilem amorem firmare: & a quam plurimis infirmitatibus custodire.
units.tr: Andromeda is the image of a girl with loose hair and her hands relaxed. She is held by the Bull in the northern part of the sky, and her nature is that of Venus. Her virtue, if she is carved in stone, is to reconcile quarrels and disputes arising between husband and wife, to firm up a lasting love, and to guard against very many illnesses.

units.la: Perseus, ensem in dextra manu, in sinistra caput Gorgonis habens, imago est, ac locatur in tauro, & in septentrionali parte, vim Saturni habet & Veneris, si in lapide sculpta fuerit, ab infortunis gestantem auertit, & a fulgure, & tempestate praeseruat, non solum gestantem, sed & loca, vbi continetur, fascinationes quoque soluit.
units.tr: Perseus, holding a sword in his right hand and the head of the Gorgon in his left, is an image located in the Bull, in the northern part of the sky. He has the power of Saturn and Venus. If he is carved in stone, he turns misfortunes away from the wearer and protects him from lightning and storm. He also dissolves spells, not only for the wearer but also for the places where the figure is kept.

units.la: Serpentarius est hominis figura habentis serpentem, tenentisq; in dextra caput, & in sinistra caudam: est in signo scorpionis, & in Septentrione, naturam habet Saturni & Martis. Virtus eius in lapide sculpta est valere contra venena, venenosorum animalium morsus curare, & si lotura eius bibatur, facit venenum evomi sine laesione.
units.tr: The Serpent-bearer is the figure of a man holding a serpent, with its head in his right hand and its tail in his left. He is in the sign of the Scorpion and in the northern sky, and has the nature of Saturn and Mars. His virtue, carved in stone, is to be effective against poisons, to cure the bites of venomous animals, and, if his washings are drunk, to make the poison vomited up without harm.

units.la: Aquila siue vultur volans, est imago aquilae volantis cum sagitta sub pedibus, in cancro, & septentrionali parte collocatur, de natura Iouis & Martis, sed sagitta de natura Martis & Veneris: hae constellationes cum in lapide sculptae erunt, gestantis veteres honorum gradus conseruare, & nouos acquirere, adque victoriam conferre dicuntur.
units.tr: The Eagle or Flying Vulture is the image of a flying eagle with an arrow beneath its feet. It is placed in the Crab, in the northern part of the sky, and is of the nature of Jupiter and Mars, but the arrow is of the nature of Mars and Venus. These constellations, when they are carved in stone, are said to preserve the wearer's former degrees of honour, to win new ones, and to bring victory.

units.la: Piscis siue delphinus est imago gibbosi piscis: est in signo Aquarii & in septentrione, naturam habens Saturni & Martis, quod si in lapide sculpta sit, artubusque alligata fuerit, gestantem fortunatum efficit in piscando.
units.tr: The Fish or Dolphin is the image of a humpbacked fish. It is in the sign of Aquarius and in the northern sky, and has the nature of Saturn and Mars. If it is carved in stone and fastened to the limbs, it makes the wearer lucky in fishing.

units.la: Pegasus siue equus alatus, vel secundum aliquos medietas equi cum alis: secundum alios totus equus cum alis, & sine freno, in signo arietis, & in septentrionali parte, naturā habens Martis & Iouis: si sculptus fuerit in lapide, gestanti in campestri bello victoriam praebet, & velocem, cautum, audacemque reddit: si vero equi collo suspendatur, aut in aquâ ponatur, vbi bibat equus, à multis infirmitatib. eum li-berabit.
units.tr: Pegasus, or the winged horse, or, according to some, half a horse with wings; according to others, a whole horse with wings and without a bridle. It is in the sign of Aries, in the northern part of the sky, and has the nature of Mars and Jupiter. If it is carved in stone, it gives the wearer victory in open-field battle and makes him swift, wary and bold. If it is hung from a horse's neck, or placed in water where a horse drinks, it will free the horse from many illnesses.

units.la: Cetus est figura magni piscis cum curuata cauda & magno ore, continetur à tauro, & in meridionali parte, natutamq; obtinet Saturni: in lapide hæc figura sculpta si supra dorsum habeat serpentem cristatum, in mari gestantem felicitat, enmq; prudentem & amabilem reddit, & ablata restaurat.
units.tr: The Whale is the figure of a large fish with a curved tail and a big mouth. It is held by the Bull and lies in the southern part of the sky, and it has the nature of Saturn. If this figure is carved in stone with a crested serpent on its back, it makes the wearer fortunate at sea, renders him prudent and lovable, and restores what has been lost.

units.la: Orionis armati hominis imago cum ense seu falce in manu, collocatur in signo geminorum, & in parte meridionali, Iouis, Saturni & Martis naturam habet, hæc figura in lapide sculpta, gestantem reddit victoriosum, & de inimicis victoriam reportare facit.
units.tr: The image of Orion, an armed man with a sword or sickle in his hand, is placed in the sign of the Twins, in the southern part of the sky, and has the nature of Jupiter, Saturn and Mars. This figure, carved in stone, makes the wearer victorious and brings him victory over his enemies.

units.la: Nauis imago est cum retorta prora, & elevato velo, & aliquando sine & cum remis, continetur à leone, & in meridionali parte, est naturæ Saturni & Martis, in lapide autem sculpta securum reddit gestantem in agendis rebus in mari, & aqua, nec ab aqua damnum capere permittit.
units.tr: The Ship is an image with a curved prow and a raised sail, sometimes without sails and sometimes with oars. It is held by the Lion, in the southern part of the sky, and is of the nature of Saturn and Mars. Carved in stone, it makes the wearer confident in his undertakings at sea and on water, and does not allow him to suffer harm from the water.

units.la: Canis imago est figura canis leporini cum caudâ curuatâ, existit in signo Cancri, & meridionali parte, naturam Veneris habens: si in lapide sculpta sit, ipsam vim habere dicunt liberandi totaliter lunaticos, moniacos, Dæmoniacos.
units.tr: The Dog is the figure of a hare-hound with a curved tail. It exists in the sign of the Crab, in the southern part of the sky, and has the nature of Venus. If it is carved in stone, they say it has the power to cure lunatics, the possessed and demoniacs completely.

units.la: Leporis ad similitudinem leporis imago est cum extensis auribus & pedibus, ac si in cursu esset, in signo geminorum collocatur, & in meridionali parte: natura eius est Saturnia & Mercurialis: virtus huius est phreneticos curare & contra Dæmonum versutias valere, nec à maligno spiritu gestans poterit lædi.
units.tr: The image resembling a hare, with its ears and feet stretched out as if it were running, is placed in the sign of the Twins, in the southern part of the sky. Its nature is Saturnine and Mercurial. Its virtue is to cure the frenzied and to be effective against the cunning of demons, and the wearer cannot be harmed by an evil spirit.

units.la: Centaurus, est figura tauri vsque ad collum, reliqua hominis tenentis in sinistrá manu hastam quiescentem supra sinistram spatulam cum appenso lepore, in dextra verò manu bestiolam resupinam cum lebete appenso: in libra & meridionali parte constituitur: estque naturæ Iouis & Martis, virtus huius sculpturæ est reddere gestantem constantem, & sanum perpe uâ sanitate.
units.tr: The Centaur is the figure of a bull as far as the neck, with the rest a man, holding in his left hand a spear resting on the left shoulder, with a hare hanging from it, and in his right hand a little animal lying on its back with a cauldron hanging from it. It is set in Libra and in the southern part of the sky, and is of the nature of Jupiter and Mars. The virtue of this carving is to make the wearer constant and to keep him sound in lasting health.

units.la: Canis imago sedentis in Cancro, de natura Veneris est: si in lapide sculpta fuerit, tecumq; portaueris, hydropem non timebis, & à peste, canisq; morsu liberaberis.
units.tr: The image of a seated dog in the Crab is of the nature of Venus. If it is carved in stone and you carry it with you, you will not fear dropsy, and you will be freed from plague and from the bite of a dog.

units.la: Sacrarii seu thuribuli figura de natura Veneris & Mercurii, cum accenso igne, si in lapide sculpta erit, habilem gestantem ad conuocandos spiritus efficit, ac in eorum conuersatione esse, eosque reddit obedientes: dicunt etiam gestantem reddere ornatum perpetuâ virginitate, cum castitatem inducat.
units.tr: The figure of a censer or incense burner, of the nature of Venus and Mercury, with a fire lit, if it is carved in stone, makes the wearer able to summon spirits, to be in their company and to make them obedient. They also say that it makes the wearer adorned with perpetual virginity, since it induces chastity.

units.la: Hydræ seu serpentis imago est serpentis figura habentis supra se vrnam circa cacaput, & coruum circa caudam, de natura Sa-turni & Veneris: virtus eius est efficere gestan-tem ditissimum, astutum, cautum, prudentem, & à nociuis rebus liberum, & resistit omni no-xio colori.
units.tr: The image of the Hydra, or serpent, is the figure of a serpent having above itself a jar around its head and a crow around its tail, of the nature of Saturn and Venus. Its virtue is to make the wearer very rich, shrewd, wary and prudent, free from harmful things, and it resists every harmful colour.

units.la: Coronæ australis figura, imperiali coronæ assimilatur, de natura Saturni & Martis, in au-gendis diuitiis eius virtus est, hominemque hi-larem, & iucundum reddere:
units.tr: The figure of the Southern Crown is compared to the imperial crown, of the nature of Saturn and Mars. Its virtue lies in increasing riches, and in making a man cheerful and pleasant.

units.la: Agitatoris seu aurigæ imago est hominis fi-gura in curru tenentis hircum in humero sini-stro: collocatur in signo geminorum & in Se-ptentrione, naturam habens Mercurii: hæc fi-gura in lapide sculpta facit gestantem venato-rem & fortunatum in capiendis animali-bus.
units.tr: The image of the Charioteer, or driver, is the figure of a man in a chariot holding a goat on his left shoulder. It is placed in the sign of the Twins and in the Northern sky, and has the nature of Mercury. This figure, carved in stone, makes the wearer a fortunate hunter in catching animals.

units.la: Vexilli imago sit in similitudinem vexilli ex-pansi in extremitate hastæ. Hæc in lapide sculp-ta efficit gestantem in militia fortunatum, ac victorem in campestri bello.
units.tr: The image of a banner is in the likeness of a banner unfurled at the tip of a spear. Carved in stone, it makes the wearer fortunate in soldiering and victorious in open-field battle.

units.la: Imago Leonis sculpta in auro, Sole existen-te in Leone, Luna Saturnum non respicien-te, præseruat à calculo calidisq; ægritudini-bus.
units.tr: An image of the Lion carved in gold, with the Sun in Leo and the Moon not regarding Saturn, protects from gravel and from hot diseases.

units.la: Scorpii imago in annulo aureo & lapide be-zoar impressa, aut sculpta, Luna existente in Scorpione, sitque Scorpius in vno ex cardini-bus mundi, ad puncturam Scorpionis valet.
units.tr: An image of the Scorpion, impressed or carved on a gold ring or a bezoar stone, with the Moon in Scorpio and the Scorpion at one of the cardinal points of the world, is effective against the sting of a scorpion.

units.la: Imago Aquarii prodest iis qui habent sal-sas fas imaginationes, vt sunt melancholici, quartanarij, maniaci, oportet autem vt fiat in die Solis, & hora eius, & nō sit Iupiter combustus, neq; Sol sit Ioue altior, neq; Saturnus sit in ascendente, neque in 19.gr. arietis: 3.15.27.tauri: 11.geminorum 3.4.12.15.19.cancr. 2.5.19. Leonis: 3.13. 30. Virginis: 3.5.21. libræ: 7.18.20.21. Scorpionis: 13.20. Sagittarij; 12.13.24. Capricorni: 7.18.20. aquarij: 13. 20. piscium.
units.tr: The image of Aquarius helps those who have salty imaginations, such as the melancholic, the quartan-fever sufferers and the maniacs. It must be made on a Sunday and at its hour, and Jupiter must not be burnt up, nor the Sun higher than Jupiter, nor Saturn in the ascendant, nor at 19 degrees of Aries, 3, 15, 27 of Taurus, 11 of Gemini, 3, 4, 12, 15, 19 of Cancer, 2, 5, 19 of Leo, 3, 13, 30 of Virgo, 3, 5, 21 of Libra, 7, 18, 20, 21 of Scorpio, 13, 20 of Sagittarius, 12, 13, 24 of Capricorn, 7, 18, 20 of Aquarius, 13, 20 of Pisces.

units.la: Imago piscium, Sole existente in piscibus in 12. domo & Luna in ascendente, dominoque ascendentis & domino domus sextæ aspectu sextili, aut trigono respicientibus ad inuicem, aut saltem Luna respiciente alterutrum, à podagricis doloribus gestantem sub plantis pedū liberare experimento dicitur. Verum, & Tempus electionis in hisce & similibus figuris formandis diligenter obseruandum, maiorem enim tunc è cœlo virtutem suscipere, si statis temporibus oportunisque horis insculpantur, sic enim magis influere sidera, experientia habetur compertum. Vnde amorem excitare benevolis, odium vero accendere volens, iniquis aspectibus vtitur. Saturni igitur imaginem fabricari volunt ipso existente in Capricorno vel aquario, Iouis in Sagittario vel piscibus, Martis in ariete & Scorpione, Solis in Leone, Veneris in Tauro & Libra, Mercurij in geminis & Virgine, Lunæ in Cancro. Sic Leonis vel nis vel Cancri imago annulo vel lapidi infigi debet, Sole Leonem, Luna vero Cancrum peragrante, ita tamen, vt vterque ab omni impedimento sit liber, ptæsertim vero à radiis Saturni vel Martis. Tenendum etiam, quodlibet signum, quamdiu Sol in eo est, viuum fieri, cæterisq; dominari, effectumque eius præ aliis sentiri, ideoque semper Planetam dirigendum ad locum esse, id est, signum, faciem & gradum, quem Sol illustrat.
units.tr: The image of the Fishes, with the Sun in Pisces in the twelfth house and the Moon in the ascendant, and the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the sixth house regarding one another by a sextile or trine aspect, or at least the Moon regarding one of them, is said by experiment to free the wearer from gouty pains in the soles of the feet. Indeed, the time of choosing must be carefully observed in forming these and similar figures, for they are believed by experience to receive a greater virtue from heaven if they are carved at the fixed times and suitable hours, since the stars thus flow in more strongly. Hence one who wishes to arouse love in the well-disposed, or indeed to kindle hatred, uses unfavourable aspects. They therefore wish the image of Saturn to be made while Saturn is in Capricorn or Aquarius, of Jupiter in Sagittarius or Pisces, of Mars in Aries and Scorpio, of the Sun in Leo, of Venus in Taurus and Libra, of Mercury in Gemini and Virgo, and of the Moon in Cancer. Thus an image of the Lion or of the Crab must be fixed to a ring or stone, while the Sun traverses Leo and the Moon the Crab, provided that each is free from every impediment, especially from the rays of Saturn or Mars. It is also to be held that each sign, as long as the Sun is in it, becomes lively and rules the others, and its effect is felt above the rest; therefore the planet must always be directed to the place, that is, the sign, face and degree, which the Sun illumines.

units.la: Hactenus de imaginibus magicis priscorum Sapientum, quas eam potissimum ob causam hic enumerasse placuit, vt planum fiat ex magicæ Philosophiæ, hoc est veræ & naturalis Magiæ, non Goetiæ & Necromantiæ principiis quasdam esse extructas, quamque certum est superstitionem in multis per abusum irrepsisse: Vsus habet laudem, crimen abusus habet. Si quis enim cum superstitione ad male agendum eas referre velit, ordini diuino & ipsius artis, ex qua fluxerunt, principiis, erit contrarius, eique verendum, ne deliris superstitionibus circumuentus, delirus totus euadat & superstitiosus.
units.tr: Thus far I have described the magical images of the ancient sages. I thought it right to list them here so that it might be plain that they were built on the principles of magical philosophy, that is, of true and natural magic, and not of goeteia and necromancy. It is certain that superstition has crept into many of them through abuse. The practice deserves praise; the abuse deserves blame. If anyone uses them with superstition to do harm, he will be opposed to the divine order and to the principles of the art from which they arose. Such a person should fear that, caught up in foolish superstitions, he will turn out wholly foolish and superstitious.

units.la: Cæterum iisdem fere ex fundamentis & causis etiam nunc conflari inceperunt laminæ auratæ, argenteæque totundæ, quadratæ, vel triangulares, quibus certi Planetarum signaturæ & characteres ad certos cœli positus & configurafigurationes seu constellationes insculpuntur, pro cuiusq; Planetæ fauore atque influxu conciliando: imprimi enim, recipi, atque retineri in eiusmodi figuris & simulacris, certa specie, imaginibusque insignitis, planetarum influxum, rationi & experientiæ consentaneum est. Hoc interim accuratissime obseruandum, vt Planeta, cuius influxum quis petit, sit fortis & fortunatus, hoc est, in proprio domicilio, exaltatione, vel triplicitate, in Orientis angulo vel Medio cœli, liber à malis radiis Saturni vel Martis, fultus Veneris vel Iouis trigono aut Sextili, vel iis iunctus, directus, velox cursu, non combustus, ascendens in circulo augis.
units.tr: Besides, gold and silver plates, round, square or triangular, are now being made on much the same foundations and causes. On them are engraved the particular signs and characters of the planets, in fixed positions and configurations or constellations of the heavens, to win the favour and influence of each planet. For it accords with reason and experience that the influence of the planets is imprinted, received and retained in such figures and likenesses, marked with certain forms and images. In this matter one must observe with the greatest care that the planet whose influence one seeks be strong and fortunate, that is, in its own domicile, exaltation or triplicity, at the eastern angle or the midheaven, free from the evil rays of Saturn or Mars, supported by the trine or sextile of Venus or Jupiter (or conjoined with them), direct, swift in motion, not burnt, and ascending in the circle of the augés.

units.la: Exemplo sit Mercurius, cuius influxum si quis pro intellectu, ingenio, memoriaque acuenda conciliare sibi cupit, obseruet, quo tempore anni Mercurius in geminis vel Virgine, in quibus signis suum habet domicilium, sit fortis & fortunatus in oriente vel medio cœli: inuenta hora horæq; minuto, fiat cœlestis figuræ vna cum aspectuum delineatione, diligens & artificiosa sculptura in argento puro, quæ postea serico albo inclusa reseruatur, tiaraque ea parte qua præcise cerebellum contingit, additis moschi optimi aliquot granis, insuitur: præcipue autem de nocte, ac euidentius illa hora & tempore, quo sculptura & incoata & absoluta, operationem perficere, animaduersum est. Hoc anno 1610. Mercurius fortis & fortunatus repertus est circa 14. & 15. Iun. horamque matutinam secundam: Iterumque fortissimus & fortunatissimus exi‑stet in Septemb. & Octob. paulo ante & post horam matutinam 5. quo tempore Solem in orientali cardine antecedit in propriis dignitatibus.
units.tr: Take Mercury as an example. If anyone wishes to win its influence to sharpen his understanding, wit and memory, let him observe when Mercury, in Gemini or Virgo, the signs in which it has its domicile, is strong and fortunate at the east or midheaven. Having found the hour and the minute of the hour, let him have made, with a careful and skilled engraving, a celestial figure with the delineation of the aspects, in pure silver. This is then kept wrapped in white silk. Attached to a headband at the point that exactly touches the little brain, with a few grains of the finest musk sewn in. It should be noted that the work is most effective at night, and especially at that hour and time when the engraving is begun and finished. In the year 1610 Mercury was found strong and fortunate about 14 and 15 June, at the second hour of the morning. And again it stands most strong and most fortunate in September and October, shortly before and after the fifth hour of the morning, when it precedes the Sun on the eastern cardinal point in its own dignities.

units.la: Atque hic est modus intellectiuam potentiam memoriamque exacuendi è cœlorum virtutibus: ex vegetabilibus quoque animalibusque non parum me gratiæ initurum spero apud eos qui memoria sunt fragili & fluxili, licet ad intelligendum excitati, si remedia quædam pro memoria corroboranda, quibus Clarissimis & doctissimis viros feliciter vsos scio, quæque hactenus inter secreta abscondita latuerunt, exprompsero, non inuidens quæ publico possunt esse vsui. Multa autem iis inesse scias, quæ neque temperamento, neque materiæ vel vli qualitati manifestæ inhærescunt, sed soli proprietati cuidam occultæ asscribenda sunt.
units.tr: This is the method of sharpening the intellectual power and memory from the powers of the heavens. From plants and animals too, I hope, I shall win no small thanks from those whose memory is frail and fluid, though quick to understand, if I set out certain remedies for strengthening the memory. I know that distinguished and learned men have used them successfully, and they have lain hidden among secrets until now. I do not begrudge their public use. You should know that many of these have properties that do not belong to their temperament, their matter, or any manifest quality, but must be ascribed to some hidden property alone.

units.la: Recipe cordium hirundinum, adhuc palpitantium numero 7. turturum num. v. menthæ siccæ, puleg j. verbenæ, eufrasiæ, coriandri præparati, gallitrichi, sing. 3j. florum rosmarini 3j. s. calami aromatici, cinnamomi, sing. 3ij. garyophillorum 3j. s. moschi, & Galliæ moschatæ, fchatæ,fing.gran.vj.mellis anacardini, styracis calamitæ sing. ʒ v. quæ ex his patiuntur tritu- rationem, redigantur in pulúerem tenuem, cumque aqua fœniculi redigantur in pastillos ad formam nuclei palmulæ. Vsurus hunc ser- uabit ordinem. Purgato corpore 5o. noctib. nihil præter passulas cum amygdalis paucis & pauco pane cœnabit, prandium autem erit af- sa gallina, aut pullus gallinaceus, turtur, perdix vel simile quid, potus vinum vnius anni mo- dice dilutum. Singulis autem noctibus propè somni horam, pastillus dextræ nari inseretur, cotoq; obturabitur, sicque seruabis, non vltra quam XXX. Virgilij versus recitaueris: elapsis diebus aliquot, pastillum sinistræ nari aqua rosarum madefactum indito, omniaque, quæ lecturus es, tenebis, vel intelligentia cito asse- queris. Abstinendum vero, qui memoriam sic seruare omnino cupit, ab ebrietate, Venere, cruditate ventriculi inprimis, omni satietate, frućtibus viridibus, oleribus, carnibus salitis, o mnibusque flatus generantibus. Postrema mensa coriandri præparatum semen assumen- dum est. Inprimis quoque curandum, vt dili- genter & probe præparetur. Non quoque in- noxium erit, per interualla pastillum vnum o- re detinere ac deglutire. Iuuabit quoque pa- stillum super prunas proiicere, vt fumus probe recipiatur in nares, receptus retineatur, narib. gossypio obturatis, ne exhalet, vel etiam pa-stillos aliquot aqua lauendulæ vel rosacea, vel anisi dissoluere, frontemq; tempora, nares & occipitium circa memoriæ capsulam mane & vesperi frequenter madefacere, inq; nares linteola pura ea imbuta immittere. Atqui hoc remedium paucis patefactum est.
units.tr: Take hearts of swallows, still beating, seven in number; five turtle-doves; dried mint; pennyroyal, one drachm; eyebright, verbena, prepared coriander, and gallitrichum, each three drachms; flowers of rosemary, three drachms and a half; aromatic calamus, and cinnamon, each two drachms; cloves, three drachms and a half; musk, and Gallic musk, each six grains; anacardium honey, and styrax calamita, each three drachms and a half. Those of these ingredients that admit of it are to be rubbed together and reduced to a fine powder, and then with fennel water made into lozenges the shape of a date stone. The one who is to use it shall keep this order. Having purged the body for fifty nights, he shall sup on nothing but raisins with a few almonds and a little bread. His dinner shall be roast hen or a young cockerel, turtle-dove, partridge, or something similar. His drink shall be wine of one year's age, moderately diluted. Each night, close to the hour of sleep, a lozenge is to be inserted into the right nostril and the nostril stopped with a plug. Keep it there no longer than the time it takes to recite thirty lines of Virgil. After some days have passed, put a lozenge moistened with rose water into the left nostril. You will then retain everything you are about to read, or you will quickly grasp it with understanding. But anyone who wholly desires to keep the memory in this way must abstain from drunkenness, sex, and above all from indigestion, from all overeating, from green fruit, vegetables, salted meats, and everything that generates wind. At the end of the meal, prepared coriander seed should be taken. Above all, care must be taken that it is prepared diligently and properly. It will also not be harmful to hold one lozenge in the mouth at intervals and then swallow it. It will also help to throw a lozenge on hot embers, so that the smoke is properly taken into the nostrils and held there, the nostrils being stopped with cotton so that it does not escape. Or dissolve some lozenges in lavender or rose water, or in anise water, and frequently moisten the forehead, temples, nostrils and back of the head, around the cell of memory, morning and evening, and put into the nostrils clean linen cloths soaked in it. But this remedy has been revealed to few.

units.la: Communius est, licet à multis hactenus occultatum, quod recipit.
units.tr: What follows is more common, though until now it has been hidden by many.

units.la: Zinziberis, piperis, longi, galangæ, garyophillorum, cubebarum sing. unciam vnam: nucis moschatæ vnciam vnam & semis, in pulverem redacta condantur sacco lineo, coquantur in vini optimi mensura vna & dimidia in olla nova vitreata bene obturata, ne fiat evaporario, lento igne, bibatur de hoc vino tribus ante inunctionem diebus ieiuno Stomacho plenus & fortis haustus, similiter & vesperi: quo facto hieme ad ignem, æstate vero ad solem capitis pori frictionibus & pectine diligentissime aperiantur, vt vapores fuliginesque exhalent, ipsumq; caput lauetur aqua ruthæ simplici, postea circa tempora & occipitium cellamq; memoriæ fiat inunctio sequenti vnguento, quod recipit.
units.tr: Take one ounce each of ginger, long pepper, galangal, cloves and cubebs, and one and a half ounces of nutmeg. Reduce them to powder, put them in a linen bag, and boil them in a new glazed pot, well covered so that no evaporation occurs, in one and a half measures of the best wine, over a gentle fire. Of this wine, drink a full and strong draught on an empty stomach for three days before the anointing, and likewise in the evening. After this, the pores of the head are to be opened very thoroughly, in winter by the fire, in summer by the sun, by rubbing and by combing, so that vapours and soot may be exhaled. Then the head itself is to be washed with plain rue water. After that the anointing is made around the temples, the back of the head and the cell of memory with the following ointment, which is prepared as follows.

units.la: Florum caulium, lil. conual. liliorum alborum, melissæ cum floribus, menthæ crispæ, singul. manipul. ɪ. contusis adde olei oliuarum vnciasij. & semis, butyri vaccini maiamaialis non saliti vncias iiij. Vini sublimati fortissim. Cochlearia iij. aquæ rosarum cochlearia iiij. buglossi, ruthæ, chelidonij, saluiæ, singul. cochlear. ij. commiscEantur omnia, & bulliant super ignem sine fumo & flamma, postea reponantur in vitreo vase, insolentur dies aliquot, vt color in cereum convertatur, sicque paratum biennio viget in virtute sua. Herbæ autem ipsæ colligentur in Solstitio æstiuali, moxque distillandæ sunt, & ad vnguenti compositionem assumendæ. Triduali igitur purgatione præmissa cum dicto vnguento inungantur tempora, cella memoriæ & occipitium, mancasque calidus & quietus, donec ad interiora penetrarit, & hæc fient à principio per dies 4. postea vero singulis annis semel tantum per biduum crescente Luna: in tertio anno non erit necessaria inunctio, nisi semel anno: alimenta sint facilis digestionis, & potus moderatus, excedens enim & continuata hic ebrietas venenum est. Sed & hoc sequens vnguentum excellens est, quod recipit, radicis buglossi, valerianæ sing. vncias iij. radicis ruthæ vncias ij. redigantur in pulverem: deinde recipiantur succi eufrasiæ, hormini, verbenæ singul. vncias iiij. colentur per pannum. Postea miscentur succi & puluetes, addas medullæ anacardiorum vnciam
units.tr: Take flowers of cabbage stalk, lily of the valley, white lilies, melissa with its flowers, and curled mint, one handful each, crushed. Add one and a half ounces of olive oil, four ounces of unsalted May butter from cows, four spoonfuls of very strong sublimated wine, four spoonfuls of rose water, and two spoonfuls each of bugloss, rue, celandine and sage. Mix all these together and let them boil over a fire without smoke or flame. Afterwards put them in a glass vessel and leave them in the sun for some days until the colour turns to wax. Thus prepared, it keeps its virtue for two years. The herbs themselves are to be gathered at the summer solstice, and distilled at once, and then taken for the making of the ointment. After a purge of three days beforehand, the temples, the cell of memory and the back of the head are to be anointed with this ointment, warm and in a quiet place, until it has penetrated to the inside. This is to be done at first for four days; after that, only once a year, for two days, when the moon is waxing. In the third year no anointing will be necessary, except once a year. The food should be easy to digest and the drink moderate, since excessive and continual drunkenness is poison. But the following ointment is also excellent. Take three ounces each of bugloss root and valerian root, and two ounces of rue root. Reduce them to powder. Then take four ounces each of the juices of eyebright, horminum and verbena, and strain them through a cloth. Then mix the juices and powders, and add an ounce of marrow of anacardium

units.la: [illegible, ~5 letters] vnciam vnam, linguæ auis, id est, seminis fraxi-ni in puluerem redacti drachmas iiij. cumque pinguedine vrsi fiat vnguentum, quo inunga-tur tempora, frons & memoriæ cellula. Hoc magni viri vsi sunt: inunctionem suadent fieri debere ter vel quater in anno, ego singulis me-fibus, si segnior operatio animaduertatur, vt in quibusdam contingere visum est.
units.tr: [illegible] one ounce of the tongue of a bird, that is, of ash seed reduced to powder, four drachms. With bear's fat make an ointment with which the temples, the forehead and the cell of memory are anointed. The great men have used this. They advise that the anointing be done three or four times a year. I myself have done it every month, when it seemed that the working was slow, as happened in some cases.

units.la: Sed vt ab animalibus & vegetabilibus ad cœlestia reuertar, eodem plane quo Mercurij modo & forma reliquorum etiam planetarum vires atq; influxus conciliari poterunt, vt pro honoribus & dignitatibus, principum ac ma-gnatum fauore atque beneuolentia impetran-da, imago Solis existentis in Leone & domo decima, in trigone Iouis vel Lunæ: Vnde in his figuris formandis vnice spectandum, vt is Planeta, cuius quis sibi virtutem & influxum cupit conciliare, ab omni impedimento sit li-berrimus.
units.tr: But to turn from animals and plants to the heavenly bodies: in exactly the same way as Mercury, the powers and influences of the other planets can also be obtained. To win the favour and goodwill of princes and great men, and to obtain honours and dignities, make an image of the Sun when it is in Leo and in the tenth house, in trine with Jupiter or the Moon. In forming these figures, the one thing to watch is that the planet whose power and influence one wishes to obtain be entirely free from every impediment.

units.la: Verum, cur & vnde annuli, imagines & fi-guræ in certo metallo vel lapide sculptæ, credi-tas habeant vires, non temperamento, non manifestis qualitatibus, non toti substantiæ est assignandum, sed diuinæ & magicæ, hoc est su-periori cuidam & sublimiori causæ, quam non inconuenienter Spiritale vehiculum & vincu-lum quidam appellitarunt: hoc mediante cor-pus & anima substantiæ inuicem distantes co-pulan-
units.tr: But why and whence rings, images and figures carved in a certain metal or stone have their believed powers cannot be assigned to temperament, to manifest qualities, or to the whole substance. They must be assigned to a divine and magical cause, that is, to some higher and more sublime cause, which some have not unfittingly called a spiritual vehicle and bond. Through this intermediary, bodies and souls, substances distant from one another, are joined together.

units.la: Spiritus potentiarum occultarum vehiculū. pulantur inuicem, hac Magnes trahit ferrum, cichoriumq; motum solis insequitur.
units.tr: The vehicle of occult powers. Through this the magnet draws iron, and chicory follows the motion of the sun.

units.la: Hoc vehiculo & vinculo intercedente seu interueniente, Mercurius efficax est in hydrargyro, memoria & cogitatiua acuenda, vel debilitanda, alectorio lapide, colore & sapore mixto, Ægypto, Græcia, Anglia, Flandria, Silesia.
units.tr: With this vehicle and bond intervening or interposing, Mercury is effective in quicksilver, in sharpening or weakening the memory and the power of thought; with the alectorius stone, in colour and taste mixed; in Egypt, Greece, England, Flanders and Silesia.

units.la: Hoc vehiculo interueniente, Luna efficax est in argento & vitris, cerebro, oculo sinistro viri, mulieris dextro, colore albo, cœruleo & cinericio, sapore falso, mediocri odore, crystallo, climate septimo, Flandria, Hollandia, Selandia, Dania.
units.tr: With this vehicle intervening, the Moon is effective in silver and glass, in the brain, in the left eye of a man and the right eye of a woman; in white, blue and ash-coloured hues; in a false taste and a moderate smell; in crystal; in the seventh climate; in Flanders, Holland, Zeeland and Denmark.

units.la: Saturnus in plumbo, aure dextra, splene, vesica & ossibus; colore nigro, liuido, & plumbeo, sapore styptico, lapidibus nigris & obscuris, climate primo, orientis dextro; Saxonia, Stiria, &c.
units.tr: Saturn is effective in lead, the right ear, the spleen, the bladder and the bones; in black, livid and leaden colours; in an astringent taste; in black and dark stones; in the first climate, on the right side of the East; in Saxony, Styria, etc.

units.la: Iupiter in stanno, pulmone, costis, pulsu, semine, aure sinistra, colore fusco, purpureo, flavo, viridi: Smaragdo, Sapphyro, Amethysto, sapore dulci, Climate secundo, septentrione, Babylonia, Perside, Vngaria, Hispania.
units.tr: Jupiter is effective in tin, the lungs, the ribs, the pulse, semen, the left ear; in brown, purple, yellow and green colours; with emerald, sapphire and amethyst; in a sweet taste; in the second climate, the North; in Babylonia, Persia, Hungary and Spain.

units.la: Sol in auro, corde, arteriis, oculo dextro, latere dextro: colore aureo, croceo, subruffo, hiacyntho: sapore acuto & acri, odore bono, non excedente: Climate quarto, oriente.
units.tr: The Sun is effective in gold, the heart, the arteries, the right eye and the right side; in golden, saffron and reddish colours; with hyacinth; in a sharp and pungent taste, and a good smell not excessive; in the fourth climate, the East.

units.la: Mars in ferro, aure sinistra, felle, renibus: F Iaspide: sapore amaro, felleo, acuto: colore rubeo: climate tertio, septétrione, Sarmatia, Getulia, Longobardia, Gotia.
units.tr: Mars is effective in iron, the left ear, the gall and the kidneys; with jasper; in a bitter, bilious and sharp taste; in red colour; in the third climate, the North; in Sarmatia, Getulia, Lombardy and Gothia.

units.la: Venus in cupro & omnis generis speculis: matrice, renibus, mammillis, gutture, genitalibus, epate: colore albo: sapore vnctuoso, dulci & pingui: margaritis, sapphyro, & carbunculo: Climate quinto, Austria, Arabia, Campania, Polonia, Heluetia.
units.tr: Venus is effective in copper and all kinds of mirrors; in the womb, the kidneys, the breasts, the throat, the genitals and the liver; in white colour; in an oily, sweet and fatty taste; with pearls, sapphire and carbuncle; in the fifth climate; in Austria, Arabia, Campania, Poland and Helvetia.

units.la: Huius igitur influentię occultæ principium petere ex principibus & manifestis illis qualitatibus, temperamento vel tota substantia, nō tam absurdum quam ridiculum est, cum illorum, à quibus hæ virtutes promanant, actiones corporeæ non sint, & sine corpore (non tamen sine vehiculo) cœlitus illabantur.
units.tr: To seek the origin of this hidden influence from the first principles and the manifest qualities, from temperament or the whole substance, is not so absurd as it is ridiculous, since the bodily actions of those from which these powers flow are not present, and they descend from heaven without a body (though not without a vehicle).

units.la: Quare nulla hic opus ex sensibus mensura, nulla ambitiosa verborum pugna & inani demonstrationum conatu. Omnis Philosophicæ demonstrationis initium à sensibus & qualitatibus non peti posse, sed aliunde petenda, vel ex hoc vulgato patescit, si quis quæriat de albæ rosæ colore, vnde scilicet ducat originē, causamq; velit frigidiori temperamento ascribere, quid quæso dicet de rubra? Intybi species lacteumne iccirco succum fundere dices, quod sint frigidæ? at complures calidissimæ, vt sunt tithymali, qui eodem turgent & madent succo. Et aloe iccircone amara est, quia calida?
units.tr: Hence there is no need here for a measure drawn from the senses, no ambitious contest of words, and no vain attempt at demonstration. That every philosophical demonstration cannot start from the senses and qualities, but must be sought from elsewhere, is clear even from this common experience: if someone asks about the colour of the white rose, whence it derives its origin, and wishes to ascribe the cause to a colder temperament, what, I ask, will he say about the red rose? Will you say that the chicory sends out milky juice because it is cold? Yet many very hot plants, such as the spurges, swell and drip with that same juice. And is aloe bitter because it is hot?

units.la: Atqui in opio quod pernitiofo frigore necat, amaritudo est eximia. Et licet ex totius sub- stantiæ proprietate talia promanare conceda- tur, sublimior tamen & præstantior opifex, in- sculptor &formator supra illam in nostro my- sterio collocandus est & quærendus. Frustra igitur Alexandrei ad manifestas qualitates o- mnia referre conati sunt, quod Scalig. exerc. 318. summæ ait esse impudentiæ, & saltem in venenis decuit illos acquiescere. Videmus è naturæ gremio & sinu quædam prorumpere, quorum causæ etsi sint plane inexplicabiles nobis, iuuat tamē interea & voluptati est Phi- liatro, rerumq; naturalium industrio, sagaciq; inuestigatori, probabiles rationes comminisci, quas si non assequitur plane, non tamen rebus manifestis propterea derogat fidem, nec esse- ctus calumniatur, sed naturam eiusq; opificem admiratione prosequitur.
units.tr: Yet in opium, which kills with deadly cold, the bitterness is extraordinary. And although it may be granted that such properties arise from the nature of the whole substance, a higher and more excellent craftsman, carver and former must nonetheless be placed and sought above that in our mystery. Therefore the Alexandrians strove in vain to refer everything to manifest qualities, which Scaliger in Exercitation 318 calls the height of impudence; at least in the case of poisons they ought to have acquiesced. We see certain things breaking forth from the bosom and lap of nature; although their causes are wholly inexplicable to us, it nevertheless delights and pleases the lover of medicine and the diligent, sagacious investigator of natural things to devise plausible reasons for them. If he does not fully attain them, he does not on that account detract from manifest facts, nor find fault with the effects, but rather pays honour to nature and its craftsman with admiration.

units.la: Hactenus de admirandarum &occultarum in natura actionum principiis & causis, reli- quum nunc est, vt supra propositæ quæstionis explicationem ex commemoratis istis princi- piis deducamus.
units.tr: So far concerning the principles and causes of the wonderful and hidden actions in nature. It remains now that from these principles mentioned we deduce the explanation of the question proposed above.

units.la: Constare a omnibus arbitror ex iis quę ha- ctenus in publicum sunt à me prolata, plantas, radices, lapides, metalla, spiritus & astra, diuina quędam consorti lege conspirare, ǫ non aliun- de accidere videtur, quam vt Plato in Timæo docet, quod cuilibet rerum speciei peculiare astrum, vt polus magneti, & proprius homini genius à diuina mente fit consecratus & dicatus, vt ita quælibet planta, quodlibet metallū, ac quilibet pretiosus lapis, certæ stellæ vel astro sit sympatheticus. Sed hæc quo sublimiora, eo altius, ac diligentius à primordiis repetenda sunt & inuestiganda. Consentiunt omnes, Cœlum & omnia olim proxime à Deo fuisse procreata, à Deo vires accepisse & retinere diuinas, quibus tum se conseruent, tum generis sui propagationi incumbant. Deus enim nunc pauca admodum sine cœlorum, naturę, seminisque interuentu ingenerat, immo conditis naturæ legibus omnia per cœlum administrat: quæ enim Deus olim propriis operibus incoauit & perfecit, ea tanquam feriatus cœlo velut administro & synergo continuanda credidit, ne scilicet longa forte temporis intercapedine iam olim creatum perfectorum animantium genus deficeret, cœlitus vitalem vim immittit semini, quæ deinceps materiam sic apparet, instruat, disponat, gignendisque rebus reddat aptam, vt omni tempore vim illam animabilem & spirabilem de cœlo possit excipere & allicere, sicque continuatus fieret rerum caducarum sese excipientium ordo & feries, semine quidem materiam suppeditante, cœlo vero inducente formam.
units.tr: I think it is agreed by all, from what I have hitherto brought before the public, that plants, roots, stones, metals, spirits and stars conspire under a certain divine law of mutual harmony. This seems to come about in no other way than as Plato teaches in the Timaeus: that for each kind of thing a peculiar star is set apart and dedicated by the divine mind, as the pole is to the magnet, and a guardian spirit proper to man; so that each plant, each metal and each precious stone is sympathetic to a certain star or heavenly body. But the higher these matters are, the more deeply and carefully they must be traced back to their beginnings and investigated. All agree that the heavens and all things were at first created immediately by God, received from God divine powers, and retain them, by which they both preserve themselves and devote themselves to the propagation of their kind. For God now brings forth very few things without the intervention of the heavens, of nature and of seed; indeed, having established the laws of nature, he administers all things through the heavens. For the things which God once began and perfected by his own works, these he believed should be continued by the heavens as by a minister and fellow-worker, while he himself rested; lest perhaps, through a long interval of time, the kind of perfect living creatures already created long ago should fail. He sends a vital power from heaven into the seed, which thereafter so prepares, arranges and disposes the matter, and makes it apt for generating things, that at all times it can receive and attract that animating and life-giving power from heaven; and thus there would be a continuous order and series of perishable things succeeding one another, the seed supplying the matter and the heavens bringing in the form.

units.la: Sic itaque homo generat hominem & Sol, homo per seminis vim apparatum omnem atque ornatum conciliat, proximaque est causa: Spiritus enim calorque, qui in semine est diuinus subiectam seminis materiam ita praeparat, vt consentaneam partibus singulis permistione temperationemque, deinde vero structuram, conformationem positumque acquirat, tum demum in totum se diffundens singulis veluti gubernator insideat, neq; deserat, quas temperauit, formauit ac composuit: altera efficiens hominis causa est, & quidem prima ac princeps, quae in praeparatam materiam simplicem speciem seu formam inserit ac demittit, vt Cælum & Sol, species enim rerum coelitus immittuntur, non e materia educuntur. Quod autem a veteribus dictum est, Deum per naturas esse diuisum, & Deorum plena esse omnia, ita accipiendum est, quod vis illa diuinitus accepta & infusa in omnibus permaneat, quod diuina virtus omnibus insit, cuius vi omnia emergant, sed aliter in coelo, aliter in caducis rebus, in quibus obscurior, in coelo autem ad rerum generationem praestantior est atq; euidentior. Quaecunque igitur Deus tum in coelis, tum in terris progenuit, omnia vnus ruetur atque regit, Coelestia quidem per se & proxime, animantia vero & stirpes aliaque mortalia coelorum ope & interuentu, quibus naturæ leges tum procreatrices tum conserua-trices indixit. Itaq; animantium, stirpium, lapidum & metallorum omnium quæcunq; fuerunt & esse possunt, formas, vnius cœli formæ potestate comprehendit, quæ innumerabilibus quasi grauidata formis omnia gignit & ex se fundit, & sic vna vis & facultas præ se fert omnium Caducorum vires, vt ita cœlum nullo semine multas proferat tum animantes tum stirpes, at semen sine cœlo non generet quicquam, sed gignendis rebus materiam duntaxat & conuenienter apparet ac instruat, cœ-lum vero in apparatam illam materiam spe-ciem summamq; perfectionem immittat, vitamque suscitet in omnibus, lucido spiritu intercedente: hic enim mundi & cœlorum exi-stit vector, in totam vniuersitatem diffusus, rebus singulis simul & specie, & natiuum vitalemq; calorem impertit gignendis illis accommodatū. Is est, q; omnia continet, calore vitaq; fouet, huius vi & ope & inanima quæque per-sistunt, & animata sui quæq; generis habent animam, alia nutrientem quidem, alia sentientem, alia rationis participem. Sic tamen vis illa cœlitus demissa rebus sese accommodat, sic singulis inseruit, vt quantum cuiusque natura desiderat, quantū ipsa subiecti[?] ratio & conditio ferre potest, tantundē exhibeat. Nec tamen illa virtus sui semper est similis, aut vno se sem-per & per & modo eodem se rebus exhibet, sed alias aliter pro stellarũ statu & radiatura multiformi, quarum commixtio implexioq; plerunq; variat, tamen si vectoris spiritus vna semper est & impermutabilis substantia.
units.tr: So man generates man, and the Sun generates too: man, by the power of the seed, brings about all its equipment and arrangement, and is the proximate cause. For the spirit and heat which are divine in the seed prepare the subject matter of the seed so that it acquires a mixture and temperament suited to each of its parts, then structure, conformation and position; and at last, diffusing itself through the whole, it sits in each part like a governor and does not abandon what it has tempered, formed and composed. The other efficient cause of man is the first and principal one, which inserts and lodges a simple species or form into the prepared matter, as the heaven and the Sun do; for the forms of things are sent down from heaven, not drawn out of matter. As for what the ancients said, that God is divided among natures and that all things are full of gods, it must be understood in this way: that this power, received and infused from God, remains in all things, and that the divine virtue is present in all, by whose power all things arise; but it is one way in the heavens and another in perishable things, in which it is more obscure, whereas in the heavens it is more excellent and more evident for the generation of things. Whatever God has brought forth both in the heavens and on the earth, he alone rules and governs all: the heavenly things directly and immediately, but living creatures, plants and other mortal things through the agency and intervention of the heavens, to which he has laid down laws of nature, both creative and preserving. Thus the forms of all living creatures, plants, stones and metals, whatever they have been or can be, are comprehended in the power of the one form of heaven, which, as if pregnant with innumerable forms, generates and pours forth all things from itself; and so one force and faculty bears within itself the powers of all perishable things. Thus heaven, without any seed, brings forth many living creatures and plants; but seed without heaven generates nothing, and only prepares and equips matter fittingly for the generating of things, while heaven introduces the highest form and perfection into that prepared matter, and kindles life in all things, through the intervention of the luminous spirit. For this is the bearer of the world and the heavens, diffused through the whole universe, and it imparts to each thing both its species and its native, vital heat, suited to generating those things. It is this which contains all things and cherishes them with heat and life; by its power and aid even inanimate things persist, and animate things each have a soul of their own kind, some nourishing, some sensing, some partaking of reason. Yet that power sent down from heaven accommodates itself to things in such a way, and infuses itself into each so, that it supplies to each as much as its nature desires and the very condition and quality of the subject can bear. Nor is that virtue always like itself, or does it present itself to things always in one and the same way, but differently at different times according to the state of the stars and their manifold radiation, whose mixture and interweaving for the most part varies; yet the substance of the bearing spirit is always one and unchangeable.

units.la: Fieri igitur non potest, vt quidam existimant, mundi Spiritum, vitam statumque rebus omnibus sic impertire, vt ne minimam quidem astrorum opem desideret, hoc enim si esset, similia similiter, id est, pari mensura perpetuo generaret. Vitalem quidem animam secum affert & naturam ipsam, ac quæcunq; subierit, Vitalia facit, sed pro cuiusq; subiecti natura, conditione, dispositione & apparatu.
units.tr: It cannot therefore be, as some suppose, that the World-Spirit imparts life and condition to all things in such a way that it needs no help at all from the stars; for if it were so, it would always produce like things in like manner, in the same measure. It indeed brings the vital soul and nature itself with it, and makes whatever it enters living, but in accordance with the nature, condition, disposition and preparation of each subject.

units.la: His ita præsuppositis, quod videlicet diuinæ cœlestesque vires ad rerum omnium procreationem & conseruationem concurrant, perq; commune illum vectore spiritum intermediae inter cœlũ & sublunaria substantiæ, omnes mundi partes cohœreant, & cuncta complexu continentur, nihilq; in viuente mundo sit tam abiectum, cui non infusus ille Spiritus diuinorum cœlestiumq; operum aliquid elargiatur è cœlo & sideribus vires & proprietates, vitæque seminaria inuehens, confundens & permiscens, sicque omnibus inter se concinentibus, vt grauissimis Tullij verbis vtar, necessario omnia vno diuino & continuato spiritu contineri, hæc inquam cum ita
units.tr: Having laid this down, namely that divine and heavenly powers concur in the production and preservation of all things, and that through that common vehicle-spirit, which lies between heaven and the sublunary substances, all parts of the world cohere and everything is held in one embrace, and that nothing in the living world is so base that this infused Spirit does not bestow on it something of the divine and heavenly works, bringing in from heaven and the stars their powers and properties and the seeds of life, blending and mingling them, so that all things agree together, and (to use the weighty words of Cicero) everything is necessarily contained by one divine and continuous spirit: since these things are so truly, I ask, who would call the healing effected by the weapon-salve, by which a wound is cured even without applying remedies, the instrument alone being smeared with that ointment, unnatural, superstitious and fraudulent? Surely no one, except one ignorant of all these things, who measures everything by the senses.

units.la: sese vere habeant, quis sanationem, factam per unguentum armarium, quo vulnus etiam non applicatis remediis curatur, instrumento tantum eo unguento delibuto, non naturale, sed superstitiosam dicet & impostoriam? Nemo sane, nisi harum rerum omnium ignarus, quique sensibus omnia metitur. Fit enim illa sanatio per meram naturam atque magneticam quandam efficientiam, attractionem & deductionem, per influentiam corporum coelestium operationes suas perficientium per elementa, nec non toties decantatum vectorem Spiritum, qui tanquam medium vinculum primo ex definitis & propriis constellationibus sympathiam, & copulam seu conuenientiam inducit, ex qua deinceps vis sanatoria in telum medicatum deriuatur, unde postea egreditur, & ad partem usque vulneratam continuatur ac traducitur, tandemque actionem istius virtutis Spiritualis consequitur effectus. Nec tamen dubium, phantasiam patientis plurimum hic habere momenti, (iuxta illud Hippocratis, in medendo saepe concurrunt spes, fiducia & τύχη) tum ad balsamicam in sanguine existentem virrutem a telo medicato attrahendam dirigendamque ad partem affectam & laesam, tum ad movendum principium sanatiuum, id est, sanandi virtute praeditum, in corpore existens. Coelum igitur, quod pluri-
units.tr: For that healing takes place through pure nature and a certain magnetic efficacy, attraction and drawing, through the influence of the heavenly bodies performing their operations through the elements, and also through the vehicle-spirit, so often sung about, which as a middle bond first induces sympathy and a coupling or agreement from definite and proper constellations; from this the healing power is then derived into the medicated weapon, whence it afterwards goes out and is continued and conveyed to the wounded part, and at last the effect follows the action of that spiritual power. Nor is there any doubt that the patient's imagination counts for much here (according to the saying of Hippocrates, in healing, hope, confidence and fortune [τύχη] often concur), both for drawing and directing the balsamic virtue existing in the blood from the medicated weapon to the affected and injured part, and for stirring up the healing principle, that is, the faculty endowed with the power of healing, existing in the body. The heaven, therefore, which flows into many and into one...

units.la: pluri-
units.tr: pluri-

units.la: Modus quo vulnus curatur sine remediis. pluribus & vni influit, imaginatione, quæ semper adest, & sympathiam, quæ intercipi aliquado impediriue, destrui non potest, ad determinatam in corpore partem vim sanatoriam deducere statuendum est. Nam inter vulnus & telum est vis Magnetica attractix & deductrix, illa partem spectat affectam, id est, vulnus, hoc est, attractio fit ad partem vulneratam, virtutis vero deductio ad telum medicatum.
units.tr: How the wound is cured without remedies. ...flows into many and into one. By imagination, which is always present, and sympathy, which may at times be interrupted or hindered but cannot be destroyed, it must be held that the healing power is led into a determined part of the body. For between the wound and the weapon there is a magnetic force that attracts and draws: it looks toward the affected part, that is the wound, so that the attraction is made to the wounded part, while the drawing of the power is toward the medicated weapon.

units.la: Verum obiicitur, spatium interueniens, tempus, & locus, quæ istam deductionem, sanationemq; impediant, nec admittant, nihil enim vltra determinatum agere spatium, item corpus à corpore sanando tangi necesse est, tangere enim se proprie dicuntur, quorum extremitates seu fines sunt simul. Iam autem sola corpora tenent superficies. Ergo sola corpora se tangunt. Talis autem contactus non fit inter vulnus & telum medicatum, ergo sanatio quoq; per illud impostoria est & Magica.
units.tr: But it is objected that the intervening space, the time and the place, hinder and do not admit this drawing and healing. For nothing acts beyond its determined space; likewise a body must be touched by the body it heals, since things are said properly to touch when their extremities or boundaries are together. Now only bodies have surfaces. Therefore only bodies touch one another. But no such contact takes place between the wound and the medicated weapon; therefore the healing through it is also fraudulent and magical.

units.la: Præcipui hi sunt arietes, quibus pars aduersa & sensuales Philosophi ad euertendum, ad explodendum, naturæq; finibus excludendum miraculosum vnguenti armarii effectum vitiatur. Sed facilis occursus est. Et miseret me eorum. Quis enim nescit multa ex interuallo exercere actionem suam, quorum scilicet superficies nullo modo coniungi possunt, & nihilominus sunt simul, vt Sol & hominis corpus, q̄ susuperficiebus licet coniungi non possunt, radiis tamen intermediis coniunguntur, non enim potest physicum agens agere in extremum quin prius agat in medium, cum omnis actio physica fiat per contactum. Idem Sol per orbem Lunæ calefacit mundum inferiorem, licet neq; ipsum tangat, neque sphæram Lunæ calefaciat. Sic omnia illa corpora, inter quæ est sympathia & antipathia, mutuo se afficiunt, exercentque operationes suas citra vllum visibilem contactum, id est, vnius virtus defertur ad alterum mediante Spiritu intercedente, ita, vt licet spatium sit maximū, citra tamen vllam alterationem nec ventis dissipetur, nec etiam aëre vasto, humido, frigidoue rapiatur atque discutiatur, sed propter naturalem communionem, similitudinem nexumque conseruetur atque continuetur.
units.tr: These are the chief battering-rams with which the opposing side and the sensual philosophers try to overthrow, explode and exclude from the limits of nature the marvellous effect of the weapon-salve. But the answer is easy, and I pity them. For who does not know that many things exert their action from a distance, whose surfaces can in no way be joined, and yet are together? Such are the sun and the human body, which cannot be joined by their surfaces, yet are joined by intervening rays; for a physical agent cannot act on the extremity without first acting on what lies between, since every physical action takes place by contact. The sun, through the orb of the moon, warms the lower world, although it neither touches the moon nor warms the lunar sphere.
